By creating a movement representative of the full diversity of our county and the immense value that different experiences and perspectives bring, nature will benefit, leaving a lasting legacy for people and wildlife."

column2: "Living Heritage: Preserving Traditional Knowledge Through Community Connection"
column3:
"Living Vital aims to reinvent how communities preserve and share heritage knowledge by creating an inclusive therapeutic space where traditional wisdom meets contemporary wellbeing needs. We envision transforming lives through nature-based heritage practices that honour diverse cultural traditions while building resilient community connections.
Our vision is to expand our already thriving community garden where refugees, LGBTQ+ individuals, those experiencing mental health challenges, and local residents unite to preserve endangered plant varieties, master traditional growing techniques, and share ancestral knowledge. We demonstrate that heritage preservation thrives through diversity - from drought-adapted techniques brought by refugees to local Sussex traditions.
We aim to rebuild essential community bonds that once sustained societies through mutual support and collective land stewardship. By integrating therapeutic interventions with hands-on heritage skills like organic growing, cob oven building and woodworking, we're creating new models of community resilience that address modern challenges while honouring timeless wisdom for future generations."

column2: "Reimagining Railways: Interpreting the Locomotive Collection at Leeds Industrial Museum"
column3: "Leeds Industrial Museum will reinterpret its nationally significant Locomotive and Railway Collection through the creation of a new Railway Gallery. Closed for more than a decade, this space will reopen as an accessible, co-curated gallery that connects Leeds’ industrial innovation to global stories of people, place and the environment. The project will conserve and display large objects, improve access and environmental sustainability, and embed new approaches to inclusive storytelling. Working with community partners, academics and volunteers, the museum will co-produce displays that reflect diverse experiences of industry, labour and empire, while inspiring pride and curiosity in local heritage. The project will also strengthen the museum’s organisational sustainability by revitalising public areas, increasing visitor numbers, and supporting skills development for staff and volunteers. In doing so, it will ensure that Leeds’ unique railway heritage is relevant, engaging and sustainable for future generations."

"We would like to engage a part of our community that has previously been underserved. We want to ensure that the heritage of the Irish community in Leeds is saved, by working with the males of that community to capture the stories of their lives and their contributions to the city of Leeds. We aim to do this by using digital heritage, giving them skills and working alongside them to ensure that their own personal history is accessible and can be shared among both their community and their families. We want to amplify voices that have not been given the opportunity to talk about their heritage, their lives, challenges and achievements and ensure that these are saved and made accessible for future generations. We want to ensure that the history of the Irish community in Leeds is heard and celebrated."
column14: Leeds Irish Health and Homes Limited

column3:
"This project will empower local people in one of York’s most deprived wards to connect with the heritage and places that shape their identity. It will expand the role of communities in identifying and documenting the heritage that defines York and is used by local decision-makers. Although York is renowned for archaeology, medieval architecture and major industries, local communities have become disconnected from the heritage they recognise and value. Our project will enrich and diversify the city’s heritage identity by reflecting community-led connections to place and informing future planning through improved tools such as the Local Heritage List and the Historic Environment Record.

Focusing on Acomb and Westfield with strong but overlooked heritage, we will support local people to research, express and celebrate their stories. Through co-creation, we will develop local heritage ambassadors to sustain this work. York Civic Trust will use the project’s learning to extend this model citywide."

column2: "Cumbrian Heroes: Celebrating Cumbria’s Rugby Union  heritage and county honours from 1882 to the present day"
column3:
"This project will document, celebrate, and preserve the heritage of Rugby Union in Cumbria by telling the story of every player who has represented the county since 1882—a story never fully told before.

We will create a publicly accessible Cumbria Rugby Heritage Database, assigning official heritage numbers to all capped players. This will honour their contribution and protect a vital part of Cumbria’s sporting identity.

Working with the 21 community clubs in Cumbria, local historians, and heritage enthusiasts, we will gather, verify, and share historical records through the Cumbria Rugby Football Union (CRFU) website.

The project will also engage young people through intergenerational activities, linking them with former players and supporters. A network of volunteer “club historians” will ensure ongoing research and contributions.

By preserving and celebrating this legacy, the project will strengthen community pride and keep Cumbria’s rugby story alive for future generations."

column2: "#LC Landscape Connections Scoping the Coast to Coast Nature Trail"
column3:
"Our vision is a bold, landscape-scale transformation, connecting and driving nature’s recovery across England’s cherished upland landscapes.
Inspired by the designation of the Coast to Coast Path (C2C) as a National Trail, we have a rare opportunity to harness national attention and local action; developing a vital ecological corridor connecting three National Parks, a National Landscape, two Heritage Coasts and the important areas between them.

This corridor encompasses tens of thousands of hectares of highly designated yet under-optimal habitats, offering exceptional potential for landowners, managers and organisations to deliver on the ‘30by30’ ambition for nature recovery and connectivity.

28,000 people live within a short walk of the C2C, and thousands travel its full length annually. We will harness this reach: connecting communities, removing barriers, inspiring visitors, and mobilising action for wildlife. 

This project will be a catalyst for thriving nature; weaving together landscapes and a legacy that endures for generations."

column2: "Dyevolution – a discovery of textile colour and sustainability"
column3: "Dyevolution will research, protect and celebrate hidden physical, social and industrial heritage recently discovered in six original dye ledgers at Sunny Bank Mills. Previously undiscovered dye samples reveal a pivotal point in the UK’s textile industry - the transition from using natural to synthetic dyes, a significant moment in the industry’s history. Exploration of this physical heritage will reveal the stories of a largely unknown aspect of textile history – the dyeing process - and the untold stories about the technology, the work force and contributors to UK’s world renown textile industry. An engagement programme, informed by research and analysis and the stories this will reveal, will connect more to this important social, cultural and industrial heritage. The project will contribute to understanding the past and future environmental impact of the textile industry and save heritage that is at risk of being lost for future generations."
column14: Sunny Bank Mills Museum and Archive Limited

column2: "St Oswalds West End Reordering and Social History Project"
column3:
"The project has 3 main purposes.

The first is to make the listed church a more comfortable and usable space for community and religious purposes.  It currently lacks toilets or kitchen facilities and is very cold in the winter.  The project will provide enhanced heating and a disabled toilet, a new internal porch, and a kitchenette. 

The second is to gather, present and preserve information about the social history of the church and how this has changed as the community of Fulford has grown from a village into a large suburb.  Photographs, programmes and other documents about past events will be sought and placed in a permanent digital archive.  Also oral histories will be taken, including from recent refugee arrivals.

The third purpose is to inform and educate the wider community about the heritage of the church -both physical and non-physical- through a series of events, publications and digital material."
column14: The Parochial Church Council Of The Ecclesiastical Parish Of Fulford, York

column2: "The Golcar Chapel Heritage Restoration & Sensory Garden Project"
column3:
"The 'Golcar Chapel Heritage & Sensory Garden Project' is about rescuing a neglected piece of local history and giving it a new purpose. We are transforming the dilapidated graveyard from a liability into a fully accessible community asset.

Our main goal is to save the site from ruin by repairing the crumbling boundary walls and stabilising unsafe pathways. At the same time, we are creating a 'Sensory Heritage Garden' designed with adults with learning disabilities, people who are too often unable to access historic environments.

We will install wheelchair-accessible paths and sensory zones to create a safe, therapeutic green space. This work will be delivered by our volunteers working side-by-side with our service users. We are determined to keep this site as a 'living' part of the village, ensuring our local heritage is preserved and accessible to everyone, regardless of their physical ability."

column2: "St Leger 250: Celebrating Doncaster’s Horse Racing Heritage"
column3:
"Heritage Doncaster, with Doncaster Racecourse, Get Doncaster Moving, Visit Doncaster, Doncaster Archives, the Doncaster Civic Trust and a range of community partners, will deliver a year-long programme marking the 250th anniversary of the St Leger.

This dynamic project will celebrate the history and enduring significance of the St Leger, and its Georgian origins. Exploring the profound influence horse racing has had, and continues to have, on Doncaster's cultural and economic identity. 

We will bridge the worlds of heritage and sport.

Through informative and engaging activities, co-creation, preserving living memories and storytelling, we aim to inspire new audiences to connect with their heritage and rediscover the excitement and legacy of the St Leger and horse racing. We want Doncaster communities to fall in love with the St Leger again through the lens and learning provided by its history."

column2: "Doncaster on Stage: Uncovering 250 Years of Theatre in Doncaster"
column3:
"We want to uncover, explore and celebrate the largely forgotten heritage of theatre in Doncaster, tracing its story from the opening of the city’s first theatre 250 years ago to the present day. By researching overlooked histories and gathering new information, insights and perspectives, we aim to shine a light on the richness&diversity of Doncaster’s theatrical past and highlight the enduring role that performance has played in bringing communities together and fostering civic pride.
Our work will culminate in a creative reimagining of Doncaster’s performance heritage: a series of scenes inspired by real people, historic events&lived experience. This collaborative artistic response will bring people from different backgrounds together to explore, understand&celebrate the city’s cultural heritage.
This project will strengthen knowledge of local history in Doncaster, and by capturing memories and finding in the local archive we'll ensure the project finding&exploration will serve as a historical legacy to inspire&inform future generations."

"Our Heritage project envisions Little Germany as the Destination it was always meant to be – Bradford’s Cultural Gateway. At the very heart of our city, Little Germany stands as a living testament to creativity, commerce and community – a place where architecture tells stories of ambition, artistry and resilience. Over the next five years, we will unite custodians of our heritage – from local residents and property owners to cultural organisations and grant funders – to celebrate and safeguard this extraordinary district. Together, we will restore and reimagine 30 Chapel Street, support the regeneration of vital historic spaces, and champion the social and built heritage that defines our shared identity. Our mission is not just to preserve the past but to inspire the future, ensuring Little Germany continues to thrive as a vibrant, welcoming Destination where history, culture and innovation meet for generations to come."
column11: National Lottery Heritage Grants £250,000 to £10 million

column3:
"Our vision is to open up the UK’s natural and cultural heritage to people who rarely get the chance to experience it. Many BAME communities especially South Asian and low income groups feel disconnected from landscapes, walking routes and the stories behind them. We want to change that.

Rooting for Heritage Routes will help people feel confident outdoors and understand the heritage held in places like the Lake District, Peak District and Yorkshire Dales. Through a mix of workshops, local walks, camping weekends and YHA residentials participants will learn new skills, discover the history of the land and see how their own stories connect.
Our aim is to build pride, improve wellbeing and make heritage feel like it belongs to everyone and for them to grow into natural heritage ambassadors who can lead others, shape activities and pass on a love of the outdoors to their families and communities."

"The Hunslet Club: Past, Present, Future will celebrate and share over 85 years (1940–2025) of the Club’s history while strengthening its role within today’s diverse communities in South Leeds. At the heart of the project is a co-created public mural, a bold, permanent artwork celebrating the Club’s heritage and imagining its future.

A specialist mural team will work with staff, members and young people through structured workshops and community forums to shape the mural’s content. Young people will lead the creative process, gathering stories, conducting interviews and digitising photographs and documents to create an accessible digital archive, supported by alumni and heritage partners.

The stories collected will also inform permanent corridor displays and heritage open days. The legacy will be a community-owned artwork, stronger intergenerational connections, and an organisation better equipped to share its story and plan for the future."

column2: "Voices of Leeds: Queer Heritage Through Time"
column3:
"Our project aims to create an audio archive of LGBTQ+ history in Leeds, retold from the perspective of the young trans people at The Hangout. By exploring the stories, experiences, and legacies of LGBTQ+ communities in the city, we want to build meaningful connections between the past and the present, helping young people understand the struggles and achievements that have shaped their community.

Through this project, twenty young people from Seacroft will engage with sound in creative ways using archival recordings, field recordings, and DJing skills to produce a multi-layered audio archive. Participants will learn how to collect, interpret, and remix historical materials, creating new narratives that reflect their experiences and perspectives.

The project will empower young people to explore and celebrate Leeds LGBTQ+ history in a participatory way, while building confidence, technical skills, and a stronger sense of connection to both their local community and its rich LGBTQ+ heritage."

column2: "CIVIC150: A Barnsley Civic reconnected with its past and restored for its future"
column3:
"The CIVIC150 programme will reconnect Barnsley Civic with its rich historic narrative and remind the communities of Barnsley of their central role in its shared story. 

 

The two-year Birthday celebration will include talks, exhibitions and performances highlighting the hidden histories of fifteen decades. A large-scale public donation campaign will uncover lost heritage, telling the story of Barnsley through the lens of its treasured Civic Hall. 

 

Targeted capital investment will pull back modern grey carpets to reveal the original 1877 tiles beneath. Building heritage research will inform a decorative revival, splashing much needed colour across our white walls. Improved entrance doors, and the reopening of our grand double staircase, will deliver better heritage access, while reducing energy usage. 

 

At the end of the programme Barnsley Civic will be reconnected with its social and architectural history, and once more look and feel like the emotional and cultural heart of this great town."

column2: "Exploring & Belonging: local heritage and global diversity"
column3: "The 2033 Heritage strategy envisions heritage as broad and inclusive. This project helps to facilitate this by enabling forced migrant engagement with local heritage in Britain. Each year, thirty asylum seekers and refugees (90 over the life of the project) will work with heritage and community organisations to conduct research and produce content which will help to shape local ideas of heritage, while simultaneously developing English and other employment-related skills. Project outputs include a website offering diverse ESOL learning resources focused on heritage themes in 6 localities across Yorkshire & Humber, co-produced by participants, MESH and project partners, plus guidance on how to develop heritage projects with ESOL classes across the country. Co-produced local exhibitions and community engagement sessions are also key outputs. The project team includes at least 2 forced migrant experts by experience, enabling them to gain experience relevant to employment in the UK heritage sector."

column2: "Bringing the Past to Life: Exploring Identity, Culture and  History in the Modern World"
column3:
"The primary objective of this project is to ensure the
preservation of the ROMA history, culture, and heritage for the
coming decades, ensuring that they are not overlooked or
forgotten. Throughout numerous centuries, the Roma
community has been compelled to conceal their true identity
as a result of pervasive segregation and discrimination,
leading to the unfortunate loss of the Romani language and
the forgetting of their roots and history by many Roma
individuals. Our intention with this initiative is to revive what
has been neglected, fill in the gaps, preserve and pass on to
future generations and raise awareness of these important
facets."

column2: "Opening up the Saltaire Collection: The pathway to accreditation, access and engagement for all."
column3:
"This project will unlock public access to the internationally significant Saltaire Collection by creating permanent, community-led exhibition spaces and secure storage.
The project will transform how people engage with Saltaire’s heritage, increase participation by collaborating with local communities to co-create inspiring spaces, share diverse stories and create fit-for-purpose storage to safeguard the collection.
The project marks a major step-change in our journey towards achieving accreditation, enabling wider access, learning, and connection to Saltaire’s UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Collection holds over 7,000 objects telling the powerful story of Saltaire’s founding in 1853 by Sir Titus Salt and its continuing social, industrial and cultural legacy. Currently, this heritage is inaccessible and at risk due to inadequate storage. 
By relocating the Collection into new publicly accessible spaces at Shipley College, the project will deliver free public access, community-led exhibitions, volunteering opportunities, learning programmes, and will improve our long-term organisational resilience"
column14: The Saltaire World Heritage Education Association

column3:
"The Purani Yaadein 2 project will preserve and share the lived, oral, and intangible cultural heritage of Leeds’s Pakistani/Kashmiri communities, particularly those whose families settled in the region following the Partition of India and Pakistan in 1947. Their experiences, traditions, and memories form a vital but under-represented part of Britain’s collective story
We will train young people to act as community reporters, engaging and gathering the testimony and artefacts from those who were there as well as their children/grandchildren. Our intergenerational project will bring people together to share and learn about this important heritage.
The project will share this research through workshops/exhibition events, for the 80th anniversary of the partition 2027 and Leeds’ celebrations for its 400th anniversary this year. With a new digital archive and schools resources we will leave a lasting legacy for the people of Leeds as well as contributing to national narratives about postcolonial our story."

"MHT’s vision is to ensure Britain’s mountaineering heritage is celebrated, protected and accessible to all. This project will expand public engagement with the collection through new digital access, partnerships and events, while strengthening our long-term sustainability.

We will recruit a Communications and Business Development Manager to grow income, develop audiences and build a trained volunteer base. Digitisation of key material, improved interpretation and increased outreach will help people connect with mountain history locally and nationally, including communities currently under-represented in heritage spaces.

The legacy will be a more resilient organisation with stronger visibility, new partnerships, and a sustainable foundation for future growth. We aim to inspire curiosity, support youth and wellbeing through outdoor heritage, and encourage care for fragile upland environments by connecting people with the stories, achievements and challenges of Britain’s climbing culture."

"‘Spirit of Place’ is a heritage and visitor engagement project about Cumbria’s churches. This project will help connect people and communities with their past: we want to protect and cherish the tangible and intangible heritage found within churches and groups of churches, whilst creatively sharing this knowledge with all. 
Church heritage is more than just an old building: it is the richly layered narratives of human life, culture and local identity left behind by communities and individuals in the objects within churches which they commissioned and donated.
Working with volunteers, we will record the historic, artistic, and commemorative value of those objects, research their individual significance, interpret their importance as overall collections, and then communicate the stories and legacies contained in that heritage to the public, to visitors and pilgrims, and to other stakeholders. This will make an important and lasting contribution to valuing our national and local cultural heritage."

"Whitchurch Conservation Group, a voluntary constituted community group, seeks to deliver a pilot heritage education programme that removes financial and practical barriers preventing local primary school children from accessing Whitchurch’s natural, social and built heritage. Through the Whitchurch School Heritage Programme, we aim to enable 700 Year 2 pupils from five local schools to engage directly with the River Test chalkstream and Whitchurch Silk Mill, combining outdoor environmental learning with structured heritage interpretation.
Our objectives are to improve understanding of the River Test’s ecological and historic importance; strengthen children’s connection to place; and support Whitchurch Silk Mill’s charitable aim to widen educational access at a time when it lacks capacity to fund outreach independently. The project also aims to extend the legacy of previous National Lottery Heritage Fund investment in local river and industrial heritage, embedding learning, stewardship and responsible access at an early age through a partnership-led, curriculum-aligned programme."

column2: "TPT - Preserving the Past, Enriching the Future"
column3: "Our organisation aims to strengthen and secure the future of the Trans Pennine Trail as a nationally recognised, inclusive route for walking, cycling, wheeling and horse riding. Through this project we want to build the capacity of the TPT National Office, enabling us to better manage, promote and protect the Trail’s natural, built and social heritage. The project will improve accessibility, expand public, educational and digital engagement, and raise awareness of environmental sustainability and climate change. By investing in staff capacity, partnerships and digital infrastructure, we aim to create a more resilient organisation and a well-managed, welcoming Trail. The long-term legacy will be a healthier, more connected, and sustainable green corridor that benefits communities now and safeguards the Trail for future generations."

column2: "The 1932 Centenary Lounge: Creating a New Home for our Sporting Heritage."
column3: "Our organisation aims to preserve, celebrate, and share the rich heritage of Sheffield Tigers RUFC and its deep roots within the Sheffield community. Through the redevelopment of the 1932 Lounge, we want to transform a historically significant space into an accessible, engaging, and community-focused heritage hub. The project will protect important stories, memorabilia, and traditions while creating new opportunities for learning, participation, and connection. We aim to involve supporters, local residents, schools, and volunteers in shaping and interpreting this shared history, ensuring it reflects a wide range of voices and experiences. By combining conservation, digital interpretation, and community programming, we hope to inspire pride, strengthen identity, and make our heritage relevant for future generations. Ultimately, we want the 1932 Lounge to become a living space where history is not only preserved but actively experienced and enjoyed."

"Archipelago will deliver a participatory heritage programme exploring the legacy of the Luddite Uprisings and their contemporary relevance, marking the 215th anniversary of this pivotal socio-industrial history. In partnership with Leeds Industrial Museum (LIM), the project responds to gaps in public understanding of Luddism and connects contemporary debates of technology, labour and workers’ rights.

Through oral history gathering, heritage craft skill-sharing - including textiles and folk songs - and accessible digital storytelling tools, over 300 participants will explore how technological change has shaped work from 1811 to now.

The project will generate new heritage material, informing interpretation and contributing to LIM’s exhibition programme, generating six new permanent collection items, and a digital archive, reaching over 75,000 people, foregrounding voices often absent from heritage narratives - including women, migrants, working-class and LGBTQ+ communities - the project strengthens public understanding of industrial heritage and creates lasting legacy of participation, ownership and pride."

"We want to preserve and celebrate South Asian food heritage by creating a recipe book that is as much about memory and story as it is about cooking. Food holds the voices of our ancestors, the rhythms of migration and the joy of sharing across generations.
Each recipe will be paired with a poem, story or fragment of history, creating a multi-sensory archive where taste and tradition intertwine. These elements will bring to life cultural memories that risk being forgotten, passing them on in new and engaging ways.
The book will be both practical and symbolic: printed copies for use in kitchens, libraries and community spaces, and a digital version, accessible worldwide via QR codes and web links. Together, these resources will connect people to heritage in inclusive, accessible ways, ensuring these traditions continue to nourish communities for generations to come."

column2: "Synth City – Celebrating the Legacy of The Limit"
column3: "'Synth City – Celebrating the Legacy of The Limit' aims to preserve and promote the story of one of Sheffield’s most influential underground music venues. Opening in 1978, The Limit became the launchpad for the city’s pioneering electropop scene, nurturing acts like The Human League, Vice Versa (became ABC), Clock DVA, Cabaret Voltaire, Heaven 17 and others. With its 50th anniversary approaching in 2028, our project will collect and share the memories, music and cultural impact of this iconic space. Through oral histories, exhibitions, podcasts, a new book, and a documentary film, we’ll create a living archive that reintroduces this vital chapter of Sheffield’s story to new audiences. The project will train volunteers, celebrate local creativity, and ensure that The Limit’s legacy is not lost to time. Led by the newly formed Synth City, we will honour the past while building skills and pride for the future."

column2: "Lifting the Lid - Rediscovering the stories through uncovering the objects. A project to capture the information and increase engagement with the collections at the Yorkshire Air Museum & Allied Air Forces Memorial."
column3:
"Our museum would like to achieve greater engagement between our historic objects (currently inaccessible in store) and our volunteers, visitors and a wider audience. Providing new opportunities for up-close and individual contact with real objects, while improving collections care standards. 
The project will focus on researching, documenting, photographing and re-storing around 7000 small objects and personal archives currently jumbled together in 232 boxes. To do this we need to install a Spectrum compliant Collections Management System to improve catalogue records and some bespoke racking to improve care and make items more 'visible' for store tours. New engagement programmes will trial ways of taking our collection out to new users and making it more accessible and interactive on site."
column14: The Yorkshire Air Museum and Allied Air Forces Memorial Limited

column3:
"Common Grounding will create the first community-led archive documenting life at Napier Barracks, Folkestone - the recently-closed asylum seeker accommodation that shaped our town from 2020-2025. Working with people who lived/worked/volunteered at the Barracks, we will gather digital ephemera, objects, recordings and personal testimonies, commencing during Refugee Week 2026 and moving beyond.
Our vision is to place the people most affected by the Barracks at the centre of how its history is told and remembered, creating a polyphonal, community-owned record before memories and materials are lost. In partnership with SOAS University of London, we will develop rigorous archival methodology rooted in best practice.
The legacy will be a digital archive hosted by the SOAS team that honestly reflects the impact of the Barracks on Folkestone's communities - and preserves that history not just for future generations but also for other communities engaging with mass asylum accommodation accommodation initiatives."

"The project aims to celebrate and safeguard the legacy of the Pullin family of Sheffield – one of Britain’s oldest fairground/amusements families, whose history stretches back generations. The Pullins were among the first travelling families in the UK from the 12th century and have maintained an unbroken connection with Sheffield for over 100 years. The family also played an early role in the establishment of the National Fairground and Circus Archive (NFCA) at the University of Sheffield. This project is about recording the heritage of the last two family members, restoring the two last made rides by Jackson's, creating an archive of materials about the association with Sheffield Parks: oral recordings, stories from users, interpretation boards for others to learn from: book, digitising stories, photos and a film for public use/learning, providing activities around heritage painting skills, promoting cultural diversity, ensuring a legacy to celebrate the Pullin archive and connection."

column2: "‘Breathing New Life into our church, community and environment for a sustainable future’"
column3:
"By planning collaboratively, and building our strengths as a community, this heritage project is aimed at inspiring people, developing skills, and increasing a sense of custodianship whilst bringing generations together.  Part of our mission is for people to enjoy celebrating heritage, enhancing awareness of the history of the buildings and architecture here, and environmental conservation issues. 

Our aim is to increase the number of local people involved in protecting heritage. Ecologically we will be developing the church grounds, increasing biodiversity and planting for pollinators. This project is also about improving the fabric of the building. We will replace the roof and improve the insulation in the roof, significantly reducing heat loss, and we will install solar panels. Materials will be sourced locally. All the renovations and environmental work will be documented in the learning resources made widely available in the town to support and encourage others."
column14: The Bridge Church Otley United Reformed Church Charity

column3: "Our project is entitled 'Appleby - Unearthing the Past'. Our intention is to investigate up to three sites which are from the Iron Age/Roman period and are expected to have connections with the Iron Age population of the area, building on recent work which has reclassified a local site. Very little is known about settlement in this area of the Eden Valley before the building of Appleby Castle, so we have identified some key local sites to investigate.  We have a track record of 28 years varied archaeological work and activities, not just digging but with a strong educational element, involving schools, talks, skills workshops, and training All of these will be an essential part of the project and although there is a relatively small population base here, we can show that there is a need, demand and desire for this project locally."

"Building on the success of BDHA, the programme evaluation, and recent design consultations, this initiative takes a strategic approach to increasing leadership and participation in heritage across the least engaged people and places in Bradford District. It will identify and train a cohort of Heritage Champions to promote heritage and build confidence in underrepresented communities. The programme will co-create community-led heritage projects at inception and growth stages, supporting each for 12 months, with at least 50% representing stories from minority ethnic communities. A community led heritage network will be co-designed and delivered to convene, connect and enable knowledge exchange between grassroots groups and the wider heritage sector, strengthening skills and confidence to influence heritage policy and practice. The programme will also showcase stories from heritage commissions and support communities to celebrate their heritage at an annual Bradford Heritage Festival. Evaluation will embed trained community heritage researchers throughout the process."

column2: "Hidden Threads: Revealing the Heritage of South Asian Muslim Women in Bradford"
column3:
"Hidden Threads will preserve and share the living cultural heritage of South Asian Muslim women in Bradford, transforming informal, undocumented knowledge into a recognised and lasting public resource. The project will capture traditional textile practices, including phulkari embroidery rooted in Punjab, crewelwork traditions from Kashmir, and other techniques passed down through generations, alongside the migration histories, cultural identities, and lived experiences of the women who practise them. This heritage exists largely outside formal archives and is at real risk of being lost.

Through community-led sessions, public exhibitions, and a digital archive, the project will connect people and communities to this heritage for the first time, ensuring it is preserved, celebrated, and passed on to future generations."

column2: "Sporting Heritage - the Golden Thread of UK Heritage"
column3: "Our project will ensure that sporting heritage - the golden thread of the UK's heritage story - is protected and shared into the future. It will do that by ensuring that Sporting Heritage CIC - the only sector support organisation for sport which exists internationally - will be in a far stronger, strategic and resilient position. Our project will provide us with the time and capacity to research and evidence the impact we make on removing sporting heritage from risk, creating more resilient heritage across the UK, diversifying heritage, and impacting on wider agendas. It will allow us to use this research to shout loudly about what we do and the impact we make, and to create clear investment models for sponsors, funders, and clients wishing to use our consultancy services, levering in additional funding as well as ensuring we have the best governance model in place."

"Flux Rotherham will establish Palladiums of the North as a sustainable, borough-wide model for identifying, recording, interpreting and preserving Rotherham’s social and community heritage with local people and Rotherham Museums, Arts and Heritage. The project focuses on underrepresented histories held in memory, personal collections and informal archives, particularly the social and entertainment culture of working men’s clubs, community venues and everyday spaces of gathering from the 1950s to the 1990s. Building on lessons from our 2025 National Lottery Heritage Fund project, The Sensational Alzanas and Other Daredevils, we will use creative, community-led methods to recover at-risk heritage and transfer it to public collections for long-term safeguarding. Through oral histories, digitisation, exhibitions, immersive events and digital interpretation, communities will help shape how their histories are recorded and shared. The project will leave a lasting legacy through new collections, stronger partnerships and a tested framework for inclusive contemporary collecting across Rotherham."

column2: "Hebden Bridge Picture House – a heritage fit for the future"
column3:
"Hebden Bridge Picture House is a rare survivor, at the heart of, and owned by, its community since 1921, the jewel in the crown of the cultural and community life of a special town. However, we face major risks, as well as opportunities to share, this amazing heritage.  
We face major risks of loss through structural challenges to the fabric, economic changes that mean we need new facilities to be viable for the future and urgent needs to make the cinema accessible to all. 
Our project will transform our community cinema, attracting new audiences, enabling everyone to enjoy their cinema, addressing environmental challenges, developing heritage skills and enabling our work with many groups who cannot access mainstream cinemas. The first Sanctuary Cinema in the UK, we will work with all of our communities, to secure an accessible, sustainable, viable cinema, at the heart of our community for the decades ahead."
column11: National Lottery Heritage Grants £250,000 to £10 million

column2: "St Mary's - the next nine hundred years"
column3:
"St Mary’s, Kirkby Lonsdale, is a Grade One listed Major Church, the largest community building in our rural market town and in the heart of the Conservation Area. Dating from the early C12th, St Mary’s is listed Priority A on the Heritage at Risk Register. Through this project, we will secure St Mary’s “for all, for all time” by addressing the wet tower, leaking roof and reordering the interior to create flexible, vibrant spaces which better serves residents and visitors.
We want to transform how people experience our heritage through engaging interpretation, tours of the church and tower roof-top, and reigniting cultural heritage through a new bell-ringing school. We will strengthen our role as a community hub by expanding our events programme, developing a café with the vocational secondary school and providing the town’s first Changing Places toilet. Environmental improvements and new income streams will ensure long-term sustainability and resilience."
column11: National Lottery Heritage Grants £250,000 to £10 million
column14: Parochial Church Council for the Ecclesiastical Parish of the Kirkby Lonsdale Team Ministry

column3:
"Reimagining Harewood will encourage a more diverse range of people to experience and engage with our heritage, improve understanding of Harewood’s history, enhance and heal our historic landscape, and support Harewood’s long term financial and environmental sustainability.  

We aim to achieve this through capital works, new interpretation and displays and engagement activities that will remove barriers to access and participation. A new visitor centre in the existing Grade II Bakehouse will offer accessible and welcoming facilities and inclusive interpretation co-designed with descendant and local communities as part of an engagement programme. This historic Bakehouse will be conserved and brought into public use. Harewood's landscape will be healed with improved biodiversity; and historic sightlines between the House, Bakehouse and Courtyard restored.  

By improving arrival, interpretation and facilities, Reimagining Harewood will strengthen organisational sustainability, diversify income, and secure Harewood’s long-term future as a welcoming, relevant and resilient place of heritage and learning."
column11: National Lottery Heritage Grants £250,000 to £10 million

column2: "Speaking Our Minds:  MindOut 25+ Years and LGBTQ Mental Health"
column3:
"MindOut will deliver an 18-month heritage project to capture, preserve, and share over 25 years of LGBTQ mental health history. Working with LGBTQ service users, volunteers, and staff (past and present), the project will record lived-experience stories showing how language, identities, attitudes, and approaches to mental health support have changed over time.

Using participatory, safety-first methods, the project will preserve underrepresented heritage at risk of being lost, particularly the experiences of early pioneers and long-term community members. Twenty-five oral histories will be ethically recorded, professionally transcribed, digitally archived, and shared through accessible online and community-based formats.

Alongside preserving heritage, the project will strengthen MindOut’s digital capacity and organisational resilience by embedding sustainable systems for managing, storing, and sharing heritage materials. By increasing understanding of LGBTQ mental health history and widening participation in heritage activity, the project will support community connection and contribute to a more inclusive national heritage record."

"The specific vision of this project is to reestablish the Beehive Shelter as a major historic and cultural focus at the heart of Wilsden. We will both restore an important building in the centre of Wilsden and to develop resources that will capture the importance of this building to Wilsden’s cultural heritage. 
The project will both repair the Beehive Shelter and reemphasise a link to the importance that the Co-operative movement has played in the life of Wilsden over more than 100 years. 
This project is a part of Wilsden Parish Council’s vision of enhancing the sense of place for Wilsden. Place-making is important for Wilsden, whether this is by improved management of green spaces or installation of seasonal decorations. Completion will deliver not only a restored building at a key location in the village, but also an enhanced appreciation of why it’s importance in the history of the village."

column2: "400 Stories - celebrating children, storytelling, cultural legacy and the libraries of Leeds"
column3:
"‘400 Stories’ is part of a three-phase project by Fidget Theatre in partnership with Leeds Libraries to better connect children in Leeds to their heritage:
 
Phase One, heritage research: Work with specialists at Leeds Central Library Local and Family History archives and at the National Science and Media Museum researching the life of Maud Hummerston, the first female Librarian and BBC radio presenter of ‘Children’s Hour’.
 
Phase two, community workshops and exhibition: Through workshops with local primary school pupils, including SEND pupils, and with families in community libraries we will share Ms Hummerston’s story, unlocking the archives and co-creating a multi-media exhibition exploring the heritage and value of storytelling for children in Leeds.
 
Phase Three, theatre performance: We will produce and perform Arts Council Funded “The Elf Adventure”, a playful and inclusive new show about Ms Hummerston in Leeds Central Library, and share the co-created exhibition with diverse family audiences."

"Barrow in Focus will celebrate and safeguard Barrow’s industrial and social heritage through the nationally significant photographic collection of local photographer Ken Royall. Working with local communities, it will deepen understanding of Barrow’s shipbuilding legacy, everyday life and civic pride, while ensuring these stories are preserved and shared for future generations. 
It will digitise and fully catalogue the Ken Royall Collection, securing its long-term preservation and making it freely accessible online for the first time. A programme of community collecting and creative engagement will capture memories, personal stories and contemporary reflections on what people value about Barrow today. 
A strong focus on young people, families and older residents will support skills, confidence and belonging in an area facing social and economic challenges. The project will strengthen organisational resilience through workforce development, and volunteer growth, ensuring the museum is equipped to serve its community beyond the project."

column2: "St. Chad's Past and Future: Restoring the historic Spire at St. Chads and recording stories to capture Far Headingley's culture."
column3: "This project ensures that St Chad’s, a Grade II church can undertake urgent repair work on its magnificent Spire and Clock. Every day more water is getting into the Spire. This winter, so much water entered the Spire that the Church clock stopped. We want to preserve the Spire and clock; featured in John Atkinson Grimshaw’s paintings (Leeds’s most celebrated artist from the 1860’s) and create new engagement by hosting a talk by Leeds City Art Gallery and engaging with 26 local groups. We will also gather local heritage by recording oral histories from the community via video and drones (including on the stained glass window, bell ringing and Headingley through the decades.) It is important to capture these stories now, as our community is aging and their stories could be lost. This project is to safeguard both the physical and cultural heart of St?Chad’s for generations to come."
column14: The Parochial Church Council Of The Ecclesiastical Parish Of St Chad, Far Headingley, Leeds

column2: "Glen and Moor: Nature Connection at Bracken Hall"
column3: "Baildon Town Council would like to connect the local communities of Baildon and Bradford with the nationally important natural heritage of the recently designated Bradford Pennine Gateway National Nature Reserve and the social and archaeological heritage of the local area. We will engage local communities to co-produce a new exhibition at Bracken Hall Countryside Centre, located at the heart of the new nature reserve, to interpret UK priority habitats, endangered species, and rich social and archaeological heritage of Shipley Glen and Baildon Moor. Recruiting and training our volunteer team will enable them to assist local communities to learn about and connect with the valuable heritage of Shipley Glen and Baildon Moor. We will provide opportunities for local communities, who may not already engage with nature, to improve awareness and understanding of nature on their doorstep and contribute to the long-term future of precious environments by engaging future advocates and activists."

"KAWACC’s a women-led organisation that’s supported Keighley’s migrant/minoritised communities for 40+ years. R2R creates permanent digital and physical archives celebrating KAWACC’s role in the local settlement, aspiration and growth of three generations of South Asian women.  It documents undervalued stories of how KAWACC contributed to local women’s resilience and empowerment. It shows how women struggled with their roles. as brides, mothers and widows, patriarchal cultures and hostile host communities, eventually finding their place.  Roots to Resilience: 
*makes Keighley’s South Asian women’s heritage visible for the first time, preventing their stories from being forgotten
*highlights KAWACC’s developing role as a safe haven for minoritised women
*shows how KAWACC supported women to improve their lives 
*presents stories which can empower local South Asian women today
*shares this heritage across local communities
*embeds heritage skills within local communities, enabling them to preserve new community stories as they emerge."
column14: Keighley Association For Women And Children's Centre

column2: "Collections Reimagined: Preserving Our Past, Protecting Our Future."
column3:
"This project will address longstanding challenges in collections storage at BDMG by identifying the most suitable long-term solution and exploring community interest in how heritage is cared for and accessed. Through feasibility studies, consultation, and sector research, we aim to develop a clear, sustainable plan for safeguarding Bradford’s reserve collections and enhancing public access.
The legacy of this project will be a permanent, environmentally sustainable home for the reserve collections, enabling deeper engagement with communities and greater representation of Bradford’s diverse heritage. It will unlock space across our four museum sites, improving their functionality and economic sustainability. A new facility will also create opportunities for income generation, education, and community use.
Ultimately, this project will strengthen BDMG’s resilience, support long-term strategic planning, and ensure that Bradford’s heritage is protected, celebrated, and accessible for generations to come."
column14: City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council

column3:
"Two events 800 years ago - a 1227 royal market charter and a bridge over the Wharfe in 1228 - transformed Otley forever, enabling the trade, industrial and cultural traditions that have shaped Otley’s distinctive, vibrant community.

Otley 800 celebrates that story. Led by Otley Town Council and running from May 2027 - June 2028, it will bring together thousands of residents of all ages and backgrounds to discover, celebrate and take pride in their heritage.

Five strands bring Otley's history to life: Charter Weekend celebration; People's Tapestry created by 150 volunteers; pop-up museum reuniting residents with a collection unseen for 16 years; community grants programme; and Bridge Weekend closing celebration.

The enduring legacy will be a town better equipped to celebrate its heritage - inspired residents, strengthened community groups, new heritage volunteers and the skills, partnerships and knowledge to invest in and preserve Otley's heritage for generations to come."

"In 2027, the Thackray Museum of Medicine will celebrate its 30th anniversary. Our Grade II listed Victorian Workhouse building is now a significant heritage risk, threatening our 80,000 item collection and the organisation’s sustainability. Over the past three decades, we have become deeply rooted in our local community, undertaking vital work that must continue. Our positioning to ‘help shape a better tomorrow’ – established as part of our NLHF-funded Insights, Identity and Imagination project – is defined by our location on Europe’s biggest teaching hospital campus and within Harehills, a ward in the top 1% of most deprived communities in England.

Our project will see us devise a significant, in-depth business case to turn the problems of our physical structure into ambitious opportunities for growth and development, whilst continuing to build on vital sustainability and resilience programmes to ensure our longevity for at least the next 30 years to come."

column2: "Transition and Transformation: Securing a Sustainable Operating Model for the National Holocaust Museum"
column3:
"The National Holocaust Museum is moving from a £4.5m capital redevelopment into a more stable operating phase. The new exhibition and reconfigured site are now open, but we are still working through the practical impact of that change, including access, wayfinding and visitor flow.

This is happening in a difficult wider context. Rising antisemitism, changes in education, tougher fundraising conditions and a long period of leadership instability have placed real pressure on capacity, finances, staff confidence and strategic direction. These pressures have shown that the Museum now needs stronger governance, clearer leadership, better internal structures and more robust financial planning.

A Business Planning Consultant has been appointed to develop a realistic five-year operating and financial model. This project will help us put that model into practice, so the Museum can operate with confidence, protect the Lottery investment and build long-term sustainability."

"Archaeology Connected: Participation in Practice will help address barriers to participation in archaeology and will support the Council for British Archaeology (CBA) as we rebrand and transition into Archaeology UK. It supports our continued approach to unlocking archaeological content for wider audiences and builds upon the outcomes and learning from our previous Reconnecting Archaeology project. Since the onset of commercial archaeology in the UK in 1990, the number of people actively participating in archaeology has declined markedly. Whilst Heritage Fund community archaeology projects have provided a much-needed focus, these have remained small in scale and limited in duration. Over the last 4 years, we have developed a robust evidence base to support these assumptions. Our data is now directly shaping our response and Archaeology Connected continues our transformation to underpin our role as the bedrock of grassroots archaeology and to increase opportunities for the public to access and shape archaeology."

"The project will foreground global majority working-class histories in Darnall, a Sheffield steel industry hub, told in our own words, using culturally relevant archival practice, filmmaking and storytelling. This will lead to long-term autonomy over capture and presentation of local heritage with local, trained volunteers; establish a sustainable archive and regular Heritage Cinema Club. Ten audio oral histories and at least six short films will be created and shared at events, and City of Sanctuary 20th Anniversary Celebrations, alongside an audio walking tour.

It is important that global majority voices are centred in the story of migration to contest the prevalent exclusionary narratives and hostile environment. This archiving of cultural history will serve as an anchor for future generations and offer a nuanced understanding of race and migration narratives. It also seeks to enable a process establishing a decolonial evaluation approach that values intangible knowledge and indigenous ways of working."

"Full restoration of the 18th century Chapel at Wentworth Woodhouse, currently on the Historic England Heritage at Risk Register, as a place of multi-faith services, events, community exhibitions and historic interpretation. A significant series of paintings by Dutch Master Gerard Seghers (1591-1651) known as the Apostles that came to Wentworth in the 1780s will be restored as part of this project. They cannot be rehung without restoration of the windows, including suitable solar protection and secondary glazing. Improved insulation and humidistat valve heating controls need to be introduced to reduce environmental impact. Heritage skills training will form a key part of the project as we include the works in the Chapel within our Conservation in Action public programme. Once restored the Chapel will provide critical space for dedicated community engagement and income generation projects."

"The Save Our Spire project will celebrate the heritage of St John’s Church and the wider Ranmoor community ahead of the church's 150th anniversary in 2029. Central to the project is the restoration of the church’s Tower and Spire, securing the future of the building while providing opportunities for public engagement through hard-hat tours, open mornings and a stonemasonry apprenticeship.

Working in partnership with Scissors Paper Stone, the project will research and share stories of people who have lived and worked in Ranmoor over the past 150 years. Citizen researchers will help uncover their stories, creating a lasting digital archive through the SPS blog.

A programme of talks, exhibitions, workshops and school activities will engage diverse audiences, while new heritage trails and visitor guides will improve access to the church’s history and architecture. The project will culminate in a celebration in 2029 to mark 150 years of St John’s Church."
column14: The Parochial Church Council Of The Ecclesiastical Parish Of St John The Evangelist, Ranmoor, Sheffield

column2: "Weaving together a strategic textile heritage for Kirklees"
column3:
"This project is critical in securing WOVEN’s sustainable future as the best vehicle to respond to the urgent need to save, protect and celebrate West Yorkshire’s industrial heritage. 

We will achieve a blueprint for WOVEN’s future as a pioneering organisation delivering effectively on Kirklees Heritage Strategy, and draws together heritage, tourism, economy and culture priorities as a flagship ‘heritage in action’ organisation.

Funding will enable us to collaborate with experts to produce a feasibility study. We will explore and identify best practice models to strengthen WOVEN’s position as a stand-alone community-led organisation responding to stakeholder need. 

The legacy will be:
-A strengthened heritage sector focusing on our textiles heritage
-A vast resource incorporating oral histories, archives and artifacts
-A diverse community that is engaged in, and knowledgeable about, textiles heritage
-Skilled networks of community promoters, educators, experts, artists and makers
-A WOVEN organisation that is robust, trusted, and future-proof"

"This project aims to deepen the understanding and appreciation of African life, culture, and heritage throughout the city of Leeds. Centred on the theme 'Rites of Passage', the project explores how traditional lifecycle events are marked across Africa through diverse and meaningful rituals, while also reflecting on the idea of movement and transformation—the journeys of Africans who have come to Leeds and woven their traditions into the city's fabric. We aim to understand how African rites of passage are observed in Leeds today—how these customs have evolved, adapted, or been reinterpreted in contemporary contexts. The project will study the past, present, and future of African rites of passage in the city, connecting historical practices with the lived experiences of today’s communities. Working with African collections at Leeds Discovery Centre and elsewhere, the Leeds African community will draw creative inspiration from heritage objects and stories to foster intergenerational learning."

column2: "Beyond the walls: developing a community-led vision for Wentworth Castle’s historic walled garden"
column3:
"Wentworth Castle Gardens is a breathtaking landscape. A much-loved and safe space for people to access nature and history, we want the site to grow into a thriving community hub, shaped by and representative of the people it serves.

The historic walled garden, a significant yet underused part of the estate, requires substantial investment to be restored to life and deliver public benefit.

Through this project, we will consult with local communities, stakeholders and partners to explore how the walled garden can be restored in ways that are rooted in its historic purpose while responding to contemporary needs. Participants will share stories, ideas and priorities, helping build a rich understanding of perspectives on the site. A smaller group will test an idea in practice, building skills, confidence and opportunities for ongoing involvement.

This project lays the groundwork for an audience-led approach to future planning and design of the walled garden."
column14: The National Trust For Places Of Historic Interest Or Natural Beauty

column2: "LAYERCAKE: BEATING THE BOUNDS OF FOLKESTONE WORKER’S HERITAGE"
column3:
"Amid a Folkestone physically and symbolically transforming through culture-led regeneration; LayerCake takes urgent steps to safeguard the stories of Folkestone’s working-class communities from permanent erasure as the town reshapes a new identity. 

Built through co-development, LayerCake seeks to collectively “beat the bounds” of Folkestone’s heritage/identity-  resourcing the communities that lived these histories to identify, capture, and interpret their legacy, while future-proofing their preservation.

Folkestone Fringe brings its community-driven approaches and cross-sector networks to mobilise:

Community-resourcing: Upskill Community Curators, Heritage Producers, Accountability Panel and volunteers to drive new heritage interpretation and engagement that are inclusive, relevant and accessible to local people

Community collecting: Centre local people as history makers, gathering their stories and experiences for a new Lived and Social Heritage Collection held permanently by Folkestone Museum

Community building: Revive local heritage/collections developing a cross-sector People’s Heritage Consortium (PHC) to support shared custodianship and build future audiences, participants, workforces."

"This project will ensure the survival of St Peter and Paul’s Church Trottiscliffe by making the building fit for use. This will be achieved through the installation of toilet and kitchen facilities and making the pathway to the church level and safe, addressing the biggest barriers to visitors and long-term sustainability. 

A heritage activity programme will share our heritage with visitors and community groups, bringing to life the rich history that exists in our building and churchyard. We will be able to attract a wider range of people through music and performances and encourage more visitors to stop off at the church to seek comfort and refreshment, whilst learning about local history. We will increase our relationship with the school, offering a more comprehensive learning experience, and see people who have been put off coming to the church because of the physical barriers have a positive experience here."

"The woodlands of South Yorkshire are vital habitats for rare and specialist species in a densely populated region. They are also deeply entwined with local heritage and culture, from prehistory to the 21st century. Today, many woodlands provide opportunities for recreation, health and wellbeing, but some are losing biodiversity or remain inaccessible because of limited resources for effective management and a combination of physical and cultural barriers.
We will take a collaborative approach to increase the extent of woodland in sustainable management, working with communities and landowners to support nature recovery while protecting and bringing cultural heritage to life. Through listening to local voices, the project will reconnect people with their woods through storytelling, events, volunteering, workshops, training and immersive interpretation. This reconnection will help communities play an active role in ensuring that woodlands not only survive but thrive for people and nature."
column11: National Lottery Heritage Grants £250,000 to £10 million

column2: "Lead, Levels and Lives: the story of Greenside Mine"
column3: "Greenside Lead Mine is a remarkable Scheduled Monument, spread across 54 hectares, where the dramatic remains of more than 300 years of mining history still shape the landscape. Currently on the Heritage at Risk register, this is an extraordinary, unique, industrial site, rich in archaeology and history, known for its unparalleled innovation and human stories. It is now increasingly threatened by decay and dereliction, while the powerful human stories that give it meaning and life are in danger of being lost as first-hand knowledge disappears. We will conserve the site’s most significant features, remove it from the Heritage at Risk register and we will deliver an ambitious activity and interpretation plan to unlock Greenside’s stories both for the local community and visitors. Working with our partners, through survey, recording, and the wider sharing of knowledge, we will create inspiring opportunities for learning, training, hands-on experiences and volunteer involvement."
column11: National Lottery Heritage Grants £250,000 to £10 million

column2: "Heritage Enterprise in Bradford’s Little Germany: New Life for A Much Loved Building as a Vital Cultural and Community Space"
column3:
"This project will save a Grade II listed building within Bradford’s Little Germany Conservation Area from neglect and disrepair, transforming it into a thriving, enterprising, multi-tenanted cultural centre which is financially sustainable and rooted in Bradford’s diverse communities.
 
People's Property Portfolio will secure the long-term future of 17-21 Chapel Street through a community-led Heritage Enterprise project, repairing and preserving the building’s historic fabric whilst conserving its rich intangible heritage as an important community space.
 
Developed with local communities, future tenants, and strategic stakeholders, the project is a cornerstone in Little Germany’s development into a thriving historic quarter. It aligns with local and regional strategies, and is part of the legacy of UK City of Culture 2025.
 
By delivering this project, we will ensure this unique heritage is conserved and cared for, now and in the future, and establish PPP as a heritage portfolio holder."

"Wainsgate Chapel CIO cares for Wainsgate Baptist Church and attached Sunday School, a Grade II* listed former Baptist chapel in Old Town, Calderdale, on Historic England's Heritage at Risk Register. The Baptist community at Wainsgate dates to the mid-eighteenth century; the present listed building dates from 1859-60. Following transfer from Historic Chapels Trust into community ownership, Wainsgate must now secure the building's long-term viability while sustaining its growing arts, heritage and community programme. Placed / Displaced will bring together long-standing local communities, young people and people who have experienced displacement,  to explore belonging, memory, landscape and shared heritage through oral history, walking, making, meals, films and public events. Alongside this, an Options & Viability Study will produce a phased, costed plan for access, environmental performance, facilities, governance, income and future capital priorities. The project will leave strengthened relationships, accessible digital heritage resources and a realistic route map for Wainsgate's future."

column2: "“The Road to Resilience” reflecting our journey by strengthening collections, people, partnerships and sustainability. Inspired by the Brontës' own resilience, it will safeguard their internationally significant heritage for generations to come."
column3:
"The Road to Resilience will provide strong foundations for the Brontë Parsonage Museum's centenary in 2028 and position the Brontë Society for the future. By strengthening organisational resilience and stewardship of its internationally significant heritage, the project will ensure the Society continues to inspire future generations.

Our four priorities:
1.	Protect our Designated collection by transforming collections storage, improving environmental conditions and enriching catalogue information to ensure the collection is preserved and accessible. 

2.	Plan for future growth by exploring the potential of the historic West Lane properties and producing a Project Viability Report with costed options for conservation and reuse. 

3.	Safeguard organisational knowledge by capturing specialist curatorial expertise and institutional memory for the benefit of staff, volunteers, researchers and visitors. 

4.	Strengthen organisational resilience by developing a leadership succession plan that ensures the skills, governance and capacity is relevant for the Brontë Society's long-term ambitions."

"This project will preserve  an important but largely undocumented chapter of Doncaster’s cultural heritage by creating an eight-part video podcast series exploring it's electronic music scene and culture from the late 1980s and 1990s.

Through filmed oral history interviews, archive material and community storytelling, we will capture the experiences of the people who made it happen.

The project will create a permanent digital archive that documents the social, cultural and creative impact of electronic music on Doncaster and its surrounding communities, whilst connecting younger people in heritage recording and digital production.

By making the completed series freely available online, we will ensure that this heritage is accessible to local residents, researchers, music enthusiasts and future generations. Ultimately, the project will increase understanding of Doncaster’s cultural identity, celebrate the contribution of local people to the UK's electronic music story, and safeguard an important aspect of social history for years to come."

"Our ambition is to restore Saltburn Valley Gardens as a vibrant, accessible and sustainable heritage landscape that reflects its Victorian origins while meeting the needs of today’s community. The project will revive historic features, improve biodiversity and reinstate lost elements, enabling people to experience the Gardens as a coherent historic landscape once again. By enhancing access, interpretation and wayfinding, we will help more people understand and enjoy the site’s unique history and natural character.
We aim to create an inclusive space that supports wellbeing, learning and community pride, while strengthening Saltburn’s identity as a heritage destination. The project will build the partnerships, skills and evidence needed to support a future major restoration bid, ensuring long term stewardship rooted in collaboration between the Council, SVCIO, and volunteers.
Our legacy will be a well-cared-for landscape where history, nature and community are connected, offering enjoyment and inspiration for generations to come."

"The Hidden Voices project will capture the narratives and heritage of Autistic and Learning Disabled people in Barnsley by collecting the life stories of individuals in contemporary society and characters from the past. Project
participants will collect their oral histories, document and celebrate their life experiences, achievements and individuality. Alongside this, participants will research and explore the lives of people in the past that were Autistic/Learning Disabled.
The project will also celebrate contemporary collecting and explore the collections and interests of project participants. Exciting ways of sharing these collections with a wider audience will be explored through written text and oral recordings, photography and exhibition elements. There will be a focus on how collecting captures and reflects individual's histories. Project outcomes will be shared with diverse audiences through a touring outdoor exhibition throughout the Barnsley Borough, the creation of a project book and deposits at Barnsley Archives."

"Through an ambitious redevelopment, refurbishment and expansion of the Yorkshire Museum, we will create a financial and environmentally sustainable future for the landmark museum, the G1 listed building, and the designated collections within.  

We will do this by: 

More than doubling the amount of exhibition space 

Creating new learning and engagement facilities 

Creating a temporary exhibition space 

Creating environmental conditions so we can deliver exhibitions in partnership with National Museums  

Making the building more accessible  

Delivering stone conservation to stabilise the museum’s facade.  

Installing photovoltaic panels, air source heat pump air handling and upgrading all the single glazing 

Increasing secondary spend opportunities by adding a cafe and upgrading welcome and retail facilities. 

 

This application is to fund a Feasibility Phase to define, test and develop the project so that a robust, costed and deliverable scheme can be taken to a full application."
