This project will install a new twin artificial grass cricket practicing nets and funding will support ground preparation works for these nets to be built.

This project will provide weekly 3 hour walking sessions, over a period of 1 year. Target audiences are people living on low incomes, living with a disability/life long health condition, parents with young children and unpaid carers.  Funding will support the cost of promotion/publicity, walk leader training and DBS for volunteers, walking first aid kits, refreshments and coaches fees and expenses.

This project will deliver culturally relevant fitness sessions for women who are predominantly from French-speaking African backgrounds including refugees. This will be achieved by delivering 2 hours of sessions each week. Funding will support coaching costs, facility hire and promotion.

This project will deliver two weekly activity sessions for 11-18 year-olds and a weekly walking session for over 40's from underserved communities in Bradford. The project targets inactive young people and socially isolated adults, especially those facing barriers like poverty, mental health challenges, or learning disabilities. Funding will cover coaching, facility hire, transport, equipment, promotion, staff/volunteer and refreshment costs.

column2: Life Goals and Crew Club Hawks Girls Football Development
column3: This project will work through Crew Club Hawks FC, their community-led football club in Whitehawk, Brighton to deliver Life Goals, a four-week course blending theory and practical sessions. Local volunteers will be supported with mentoring and qualifications to become coaches for two new girls' teams at U10 and U12. The new teams will support inactive young girls to play football over 28 weeks.

This project will fund to create a sports garden multi use surface area that can be used for various physical activities and ball games for those with severe learning and physical disabilities and complex needs.

A project to encourage 100 over 40 inactive African women in and around Holbeck, Beeston, Hunslet & Armley to play slow paced Netball twice a week to help improve their physical and mental wellbeing. Supported costs include Facility Hire, Equipment Hire/Purchase, Coaches Fees/Expenses, Promotion/Publicity, Other: DBS checks for Volunteers, Transport / Travel.

This project will provide 150 young people aged 10-16 from low-income families with a safe place to build positive relationships, get active and have fun through free weekly multisport sessions, whilst improving their wellbeing, reducing isolation and providing a positive outlet away from antisocial behaviour. Each session will last two hours and will include games, physical activity and creative exercises. Funding will cover sessional coaching, equipment and promotional costs.

This project will provide a programme of dance activities for people living with early-onset dementia and their families. There will be weekly sessions for 46 weeks. Each session will last 75 minutes.

This project will purchase new equipment to be used in weekly after-school bowling sessions. Outside of after-school sessions, the club will use the equipment to offer taster sessions to juniors in the wider community. Funding will support the purchase of equipment and promotion of the taster sessions.

Taking place in Rossington, Doncaster from July 2025 to July 2026, this 12-month project offers free, inclusive multi-sports sessions for 90 inactive children aged 7-11 facing barriers to physical activity. Activities include Ultimate Frisbee, rounders, handball, cricket, basketball, and fitness games. Sessions will run four times a week over three 15-week blocks, led by qualified coaches at Rossington FC. Funding is requested to cover coach fees, equipment, and promotion, aiming to build confidence, enjoyment, and lasting engagement in sport for children who feel excluded from traditional clubs.

This project will deliver pickleball to older people in Brighton at risk of social isolation. 12 x 1.5-hour sessions will be delivered with 30 minutes social time afterwards. Funding will support equipment purchases, facility hire, coaching fees and refreshments.
This project will deliver a weekly 2-hour multi-sports session for young people aged 13-16. The project will last 44 weeks.

Sport England's 2021-31 strategy, Uniting the Movement, has a ten-year vision to transform lives and communities through sport and physical activity. The strategy has a laser focus on tackling inequalities and the ability of sport and physical activity to make better places to live and to bring people together. This investment provides capacity and delivery to implement Place-based systemic approaches, with a view to achieving long-term outcomes of increasing activity, decreasing inactivity, tackling inequalities and providing positive experiences for children and young people.

column2: CF Lascelles Hall Community Clubhouse Completion
column3: This project will enable the completion of the new clubhouse facility. This will enable the building to return to being a community facility and deliver indoor activity sessions. Funding will support the interior fit out, including electrics, wall and floor finishes.
This project will deliver multi sports sessions for young people aged 8-25 in Nuneaton. Funding is for the new activity coach, equipment and training for young leaders.

column2: Replacement roll on net after vandalism
column3: This project will purchase a new portable batting cage as the existing one was damaged by vandals.

This project will purchase batons and poms for a new majorettes troupe. There will be 5 sessions per week for different age groups. Sessions will last 1 - 2 hours depending on the age of participants.

This project will deliver running sessions, with each session lasting 2 hours: 90 minutes of running or walking at a local public space, followed by 30 minutes at a nearby centre for post community reflections. The project follows a 12-week cycle. At the end of each cycle, feedback will be provided and sessions will be tailored making the project participant-led. Funding will support coaches fees, facility hire and promotion requested.

column2: Let’s Get Moving: The Oracle Project
column3: This project will deliver free, inclusive activity sessions in Kirklees such as low-impact fitness, family dance, women-only classes, and chair-based exercise. The project which is co-created with residents, targets those facing financial, cultural, and health-related barriers to being active. 2-3 sessions per week will be delivered as part of a 12 week rolling programme. Funding will contribute to coaching fees, equipment, facility hire and staff training.

This project will support the launch and expansion of boxing sessions including specific sessions for Trans and non-binary people, people living with Parkinson's disease and youth classes. Funding is for volunteer coach training, a Community Coach Apprentice, volunteer expenses, delivery costs, and equipment.

column2: CF - Pitch Perfect - The Nets4Royd Project
column3: This project will build a two-lane cricket net facility.

This project will deliver weekly small-sided football sessions for inactive men aged 18-60. Sessions will take place once a week lasting 2 hours in a tournament style format. Funding be used towards facility hire, coaching fees and equipment.

This project will provide Step Together which will be delivered as a weekly evening and weekend dance class for people aged 50 and over, running for an initial period of 6 months. The sessions will take place in a local, accessible community venue with good transport links and facilities suitable for people with varying mobility levels. Each session will last approximately 90 minutes, including time for dancing, social interaction, and refreshments. Funding will support staff, coaches fees, promotion and refreshments.

This project will deliver a 12-month peer-led walking programme for 100 inactive women aged 40+ on low-incomes from culturally diverse communities in Leeds. Four one-hour sessions will be delivered weekly, led by a Walking Coordinator and supported by peer volunteers to improve participants' mobility alongside their physical fitness to reduce the effects of chronic and age-related health conditions, whilst also encouraging social connections to help women remain active beyond the project. Funding will support Walking Coordinator, volunteer first-aid training, promotion and insurance costs.

This project will deliver Alt Active a move breathe programme which includes weekly running alternate week sessions in yoga, mobility exercises and mindfulness over 12 months for young people in care. Funding is for coaches, facility hire, equipment, promotion, project co-ordination and travel.

column2: Repair the Roof and Row Bradford(RRRB)
column3: This project will replace the clubhouse roof.

This project will offer community based exercise classes which will be fun, light cardio sessions. Sessions will run twice a week, in 1.5-hour blocks, for 46 weeks. The project is aimed at Culturally Diverse Communities, unpaid, female carers. Funding will support promotion, equipment, facility hire, coach fees and refreshments.

This project will deliver two 2-hour golf sessions per week for children aged 6-16. The project will last 38 weeks. The sessions will take place across 4 different locations and will be split between 6-11 and 11-16 year olds. Funding will support coaching and equipment costs.

This project will expand Friends, Families and Traveller's Young Traveller Futures youth programme to include weekly sports and movement sessions for 120-150 Gypsy, Roma and Traveller (GRT) young people aged 6-25 across Sussex. Activities will include football, badminton, yoga and other sports, chosen by the young people themselves. Sessions will run 1-2 times weekly throughout the year, delivered at traveller sites, encampments, and households across Sussex. The aim of the project is to increase physical activity and improve mental wellbeing. Funding will support additional youth worker hours, sessional delivery, travel costs, equipment and engagement activity.

Investment into the Place Universal Offer (PUO) will support more places in England to develop proportionate place-based whole-system approaches to tackling physical activity inequalities. It will cascade the learning from all Place partnerships and offer proportionate support in the form of tools, resources and funding required to improve the connectivity of local systems and implement systemic change.

This project will provide a year round programme offering inclusive sports camps during school holidays for children from low income or disadvantaged backgrounds. The holiday camps will combine physical activity, personal development and healthy meals in a supportive setting. By building skills, confidence, and healthy habits, the project aims to inspire long term behaviour change. Funding is requested for facility hire, equipment and coaching costs.

This project will deliver weekly multi-sport sessions for inactive children and young people aged 7-16 from low-income households and those struggling with confidence. Sessions will be split into two age groups, 7-11 and 11-16, with two hour-long sessions each week for each age group. Funding will support coaching, facility hire, equipment and promotion costs.

This project will engage Culturally Diverse Communities women who have small children and cannot access local exercise classes due to childcare limitations and costs. The project will make use of the local outdoors and parks to support fitness, health, exercise and being able to socialise. The project will take place within school holidays and into to the start of next term. Groups will go out everyday for 2 hours, 5 days per week for 9 weeks. Funding will support staff costs.

This project will deliver a trauma-informed, keep fit and pilates class for women and girls affected by domestic abuse.  There will be two 1-hour sessions per week for a period of 48 weeks. Funding is for coaches fees, facility hire, childcare and travel.

This project will upgrade the school's fitness suite by providing a range of exercise equipment including a treadmill, stationary bikes, ski machines and free weights. The facility will be open to the community.

column2: Power Chair Play: Inclusive Sport for All
column3: This project will deliver a wheelchair multi-sport project to young people aged 8 to 16. Funds will cover costs of equipment for ten multi-use chairs and coaches to deliver the project.

This project will provide sessions that target children and young people who have special educational needs or a disability (SEND). Two dedicated SEND sessions will be provided each week, offering coaching with beginner friendly equipment. Funding is for equipment, coach fees and promotion.

This project will offer a variety of activities for culturally diverse communities across Leeds and West Yorkshire. One strand of the programme will provide girls-only football and yoga for ages 5-16, addressing cultural, social, and financial barriers. The second strand engages the wider community-boys, adults, and older adults- through football, walking, table tennis, and mixed yoga. Funding is for facility hire, equipment, instructor costs and promotion.

column2: Midlife women's home resistance training project (Leeds)
column3: This project will support women aged 40-60 to resistance train at home through small group personal training sessions over 12 weeks via Zoom video technology. The Movement Fund Award will go towards coaches fees, administration, project management and marketing.

This project will enable 100 predominantly inactive students from low-income and culturally diverse households, some of whom have special educational needs, to participate in an off-site after-college fitness programme in Leeds, helping to boost confidence levels, provide a social space and form active habits for the future. Funding will support instructor, exclusive facility hire and additional Enrichment Officer costs.
This project will provide weekly yoga, cycling and boxing for young people and adults with learning disabilities. Funding is for coaches, equipment and facility hire.

This project will create 2 new youth boys teams U14's and U15's and allow additional winter training slots. Funding will provide 3 x Introduction to football coaching qualification, additional facility hire costs, 30 x size 5 footballs, 45 adult bibs and a new kit for the new teams.

This project will create facility alterations at Nevill Sports field, extending and improving the existing garage storage facilities. The increase in storage area, by 120%, will enable machinery to be stored safely and pitch maintenance maintained to enable matches and increased use at the field from clubs and schools.

column2: Yoga means fun, fitness and friends!
column3: This project will provide 100 x 1.5 hour engaging accessible yoga sessions for adults with learning disabilities and autism in 3 day centres and 2 residential homes in Kirklees West Yorkshire. Funding will support coaching costs.

column2: Shuffle to Strength – Moving More, Living Better
column3: This project will deliver Shuffle to Strength, an 8-week seated exercise initiative helping older adults in Romney Marsh overcome barriers to activity. The project provides inclusive in-class and at-home movement using The Shuffler, a pain-free exercise device. The project will support over 50s living with long-term conditions, frailty, or low confidence, many of whom are currently inactive. Funding will support equipment costs, training Funding will support staff and participants. Coaching fees cover in person and online and physio costs.

This project will update and replace some boxing equipment and allow five coaches to attend Mental Health First Aid training courses. Sessions the equipment will support include their free community programmes, Boxing for SEND, sessions for young people in care and the youth justice system and women and girls at risk of abuse and child sexual exploitation. Funding will cover new equipment and coaching qualifications.

This project will deliver 12 weeks of after-school multi-sport sessions for inactive girls, at five secondary schools in Redcar and Eston. Participants will co-design their activity plan and funding will cover coaching, equipment and transport costs.
column14: Redcar & Eston School Sport Partnership CIC

column2: Nets Relocation and Upgrade to Support Women’s & Girls’ Cric
column3: This project will relocate the clubs current two-lane net facility and expand it to a new three-lane facility, as it currently encroaches onto the playing field. Funding will cover the materials, installation of the new nets, breakdown and disposal of the old two-lane space.

This project will deliver a free, grassroots cricket programme aimed at increasing physical activity among people aged 12+ from low-income and culturally diverse communities. Running twice a week for six months, it will provide structured, welcoming sessions led by local coaches in accessible venues. Funding will support coaches fees, facility hire, promotion, training, refreshments & staff costs.

This project will offer cycle skills and bike maintenance sessions to young people aged 10-16 based in Balby and the surrounding area of Doncaster. Sessions will include the use of ramps where young people can learn control, balance and bike handling skills in a safe environment. Young people will also receive tuition in repairing and maintaining their own bikes. Funding is for promotion, staff costs, coaching fees and equipment.

column2: CF - Brighton Table Tennis Club Moulsecoomb
column3: This project will aim to work with 300 people a week by expanding the club's after school clubs from 3 to 5 a week for children on free school meals at local primary schools with one session focusing on girls and to add a new Women's session.

This project will deliver kickboxing sessions for migrant women who have experienced trauma. Weekly sessions will run from the Common Ground Community Centre for 30 weeks x 1 hour coached session and support up to 20 migrant women. Funding will support facility hire, coach fees, project management, promotion and volunteer costs.

This project will deliver 45 sessions. 35 will be delivered outdoors in parks and community spaces, and 10 within Youth Clubs and Community Centres. The sessions will be open to up to 25 young people aged 8-18 from low-income families on a weekly basis. Although the project will predominantly focus on football, sessions will be guided by the participants. Funding will supporting coaching fees, facility hire, refreshments and equipment purchases.

This project will refurbish changing facilities and a clubhouse. Current changing rooms are limiting participation and excluding key groups. Funding is for installation of additional changing facilities as well as the refurbishment of current facilities.

This project will deliver free multi-sports sessions for children in Shipley, Bradford, taking place after school and at weekends. It's aimed at inactive young people living in deprived areas who often face barriers to getting involved in sport. The project will run across 45 weeks, split into three 15-week cohorts. Each week will deliver three sessions, each lasting 1.5 hours. One session will take place after school on a weekday while the remaining two will run on weekend mornings.

column2: Activ8 Support: Empowering Clubs, Enabling Inclusion
column3: This project will deliver inclusive training workshops, mentoring, toolkits, and a staged accreditation pathway to at least 40 grassroots clubs. Aimed at supporting disabled people and those with long-term health conditions, the project builds club capacity to become welcoming and inclusive environments. The investment will fund staffing, mentoring, training delivery, travel, resources, and evaluation. The programme will be embedded through sustained coaching support and local partnerships, ultimately benefiting an estimated 450 people.

This project will provide evening boxing and gymnastics sessions. There will be one session per week of family boxing/fitness and two sessions per week of gymnastics, split between two age groups (5-7, 7-11). A range of gymnastics equipment will also be purchased. Sessions will be delivered during school term time (39 weeks).

This project will deliver a programme of activities for men who are vulnerable to social isolation and poor mental and physical health. The project will deliver 8 weeks of cycling, two 8 week blocks of yoga, weekly walk and talk rambling sessions for 52 weeks. 52 weekly 'hub meetings' will also be delivered, each of which providing a mix of adaptive sports (boccia, new age curling, goal ball), net games (badminton, pickleball, table tennis), exercise and fitness. Funds will cover sessional coaches, travel, facility hire and equipment.

column2: Women and Children’s Swimming for Confidence and Inclusion
column3: This project will support the delivery of two weekly two-hour swimming sessions for women and children who face cultural, religious, or personal barriers to conventional swimming. Sessions will be held on a weekday and weekend with female instructors. Funding will cover coaching and facility hire costs.

This project will deliver the Deaf Active Youth Club - an inclusive, weekly after-school physical activity programme for Deaf and hard-of-hearing young people aged 8-16 in Wakefield. In addition to delivery, the project will support training Deaf young leaders and volunteers. Sessions will take place every Tuesday from 4:30pm to 6:00pm during school term time (38 weeks per year). Funding will support coach fees, DBS checks, training, travel and promotion.

This project aims to install floodlights at the club to enable year-round training and match play. The lights will also be made available to other local sports teams. Funding will support the purchase of six rechargeable mobile sports floodlights.

column2: Low cost exercise classes in Hangleton and Knoll
column3: This project will run affordable, accessible weekly exercise classes for residents of the Hangleton and Knoll estates. The programme includes three classes: a weight-based fitness class suitable for all levels, a beginner's yoga class promoting flexibility and mental wellbeing, and a beginner's Pilates class tailored for individuals with long-term health conditions. The aim is to engage older adults, people with long-term conditions, and residents from multi-ethnic and minority communities. 90 participants will benefit. Funding is required for facility hire, small weight and coaches fees.

This project will see improvements to the skate park to make it more accessible to beginners and younger skateboarders. Funding will be used to build beginner friendly obstacles and make repairs to the existing bowls to maintain safety and improvements. There will also be new signage and better landscaping, creating a safe and welcoming environment for younger users.

This project will provide Tai Chi and wellbeing classes for more mature members of the local community. Sessions will take place once a week lasting for 45 minutes and the project will deliver 40 sessions over a 12 month period. Funding will support coaching fees.
column14: The Ecclesiastical Parish of Kirkleatham in the Diocese of York

column3: The project will install two hybrid wickets to support increased participation in cricket. The new wickets will be used by adult and junior players during training and matches. Facilities will also be used during hosted regional finals, Halifax junior festivals, and Huddersfield T20 days. Funding will contribute to all related costs, including groundworks, fertiliser and seeding.

The project will deliver weekly Thursday training sessions and Sunday league fixtures at the new Myra Shay pitch. Funding will cover facility hire, equipment, and publicity costs. The club aims to provide both informal and competitive football opportunities, with an estimated 50 women directly benefiting in the first year.

This project will deliver fitness sessions using kettlebells to adults with learning disabilities. This will be achieved by 2 x 1 hour sessions a week delivered in 4 x 12 week blocks. Funding will support facility hire, coaching development, equipment purchase and promotion.

This project will provide 36 weeks of dance and movement for adults over 60 many of whom have long-term health conditions and with low household income. Funding is for coaches, facility hire and promotion.

This project will run two weekly inclusive yoga sessions for disabled young people at the fully accessible Menphys Hub in South Wigston, on Monday evenings and Saturday afternoons, over 38 weeks. Led by a qualified yoga instructor and supported by a family worker, sessions will provide adapted physical activity to improve wellbeing, confidence, and emotional regulation. The family worker will also offer on-site support and signposting for parents, fostering peer connection and access to wider services. Funding will cover instructor and family support staffing costs, with equipment funded from other sources. The project responds directly to a family survey identifying a lack of fun, non-competitive, accessible activities in the area, with yoga highlighted as a preferred option.

column2: Huddersfield Laund Hill Corsairs American Flag Football
column3: This project will create flag and walking American football teams. Funding will support for equipment, coach training, publicity, transport and admin (mostly player insurance).

This project will run accessible physical activity and regular screen-free time for 120 parents with very young children who are currently inactive. There will be 24 parent and child yoga sessions, 6 group family digital detox nature walks and a DIY toolkit of at-home exercises through their Phone Free Family Programme. 240 participants will benefit. Funding is required for coaches fees, facility hire, project management, travel for walking guide, promotion and staff costs.

This project will provide engaging, high-energy sprint training sessions designed for children from low-income families, particularly those with ADHD or dyslexia. The programme focuses on the fundamentals of physical development, including agility, balance, endurance, and spatial awareness. Sessions will occur weekly, outside of school hours, sessions will be 60-90 minutes long. Funding will support coach fees, venue hire, equipment and promotion.
This project will deliver Nordic Walking to the visually impaired. 45-minute sessions will be provided weekly for 12 months. Funds will cover staff training and equipment.

column2: Mexborough Tennis Club Playing Surface Replacement
column3: This project will enable the club to improve the playing surface of the club's tennis courts. Funding will support the surface improvements.
Funding under Sport England's Place Expansion Investment to address regional inequalities in activity levels in Swale (Kent).

Addicted to Sport is a 12-month multisport project in Leeds for adults aged 18+ recovering from addiction to alcohol or other drugs. Building on an existing programme of weekly football, running, yoga, and gym sessions, the project will add a Recovery Football League, weekly netball, and bouldering sessions across three venues. Activities will be free, inclusive, and stigma-free, led by qualified coaches and volunteers with lived experience. Funding is for coaching, facility hire, equipment, and training to upskill volunteers, with all core and management costs covered by the organisation. Sessions will run from January 2026 to January 2027, benefiting an estimated 180 people.

This project will provide free physical activity (yoga and exercise classes) for 200 people in the Sharrow community, Sheffield over the course of one year. The Award will go towards coaches (yoga and aerobics) fees and administration costs.

This project will offer free weekly African dance based fitness sessions for 14-25 year old asylum seekers and migrants, particularly from African communities in Windsor. Sessions will be for 1 hour and delivered for 48 weeks. 1 volunteer will be qualified as a dance fitness instructor. Funding will cover refreshments, promotion, volunteer costs, equipment, facility hire and project lead and admin costs.

This project will deliver a new initiative to engage 5 to 9 year olds girls in netball using community facilities. Sessions will run on Fridays during term time after school in 6 week blocks. The sessions are new and will be delivered by a Level 2 Netball coach. Funding will support coaches fees, facility hire and equipment.

This project will deliver walking football to older people and mental health football sessions. 2 x 1 hour walking football and 1 x 1-hour mental health football sessions will be provided weekly, for 12 months. Funds will cover coaching fees, promotion, coaching training, equipment and volunteer expenses.
This project will see the purchase of a 4ft Electric Auto-Roller to consolidate and level the square and keep the playing surface safe and consistent.

This project will deliver squash to young people, low-income families and refugees. 2 x 2-hour and 1.5-hour sessions will be provided weekly, for 12 months. Funds will cover promotion, volunteer expenses, equipment and coaching fees.

column2: Physical Activity For All -Adults with Learning Difficulties
column3: This project will deliver sport and physical activity sessions for adults with learning disabilities and their parents/carers/family. There will be 10 sessions of 14 new activities at different locations run either weekly or fortnightly. 500 participants will benefit. Funding is required for facility hire, activity costs, promotion and ALD physical activity delivery training.

This project will deliver Pilates sessions to individuals with disabilities and their carers over a 22 week period during the winter months. Funding will specifically support coaching fees, transport and facility hire.

This project will provide weekly football sessions for girls aged 9-15. Sessions will last 2 hours and the project will be delivered for 46 weeks. The first hour will be for under 10s - 12s and the second session for under 13s - 15s. 6 new female coaches will be trained. Funding is for coaches and facility hire as well as equipment and coach training.

This project will see the organisation extend its offer and host additional beginners classes targeted at all ages. Gentle dance and fitness classes will be delivered twice a week. Funding is required for instructor fees and facility hire.

This project will deliver a 12-month programme of layered activities designed to engage a diverse local population in regular movement. Activities include weekly alternating Move and Groove, gentle exercise, Tai Chi and weekly alternating Pilates, dance fitness, circuits. Funding will support coaches fees, promotion and equipment.

This project will deliver multisport to girls aged 5 to 16 years old. Two 90-minute sessions will run in parallel; these will be weekly for 45 weeks. Funding will pay for promotion, equipment, facility hire and coaches.

column2: Intro to climbing events for plus size people
column3: This project will run a series of intro to climbing events specifically for plus size people. The project will Identify 10 climbing walls across all regions in England and work with an experienced climbing instructor to plan and run a two hour intro session for plus size people at each wall for 8-10 people. Following that, the project will run a 90 minute follow-up session at each climbing wall and identify a volunteer climbing champion in each region to provide additional support and organise outdoor climbing sessions to allow participants to continue developing their skills in an outdoor setting. Funding will pay for coaching and transport costs.

This project will deliver 40 tennis sessions to 40 disadvantaged children/young people in Keighley from diverse ethnic backgrounds. Sessions will be split over 30 weekends and 10 school holiday sessions, in two separate groups: 8 -11s and 12 -16s. Funding will specifically support equipment, project manager, facility hire, training costs, admin costs, project co-ordinator costs and youth worker support.

This project will deliver female-only fitness sessions for inactive women and teenage girls in Darfield, Barnsley. Activities will include circuits, running, and gym-style exercises. Sessions will run for 48 weeks, twice weekly on Saturday and Sunday mornings, each lasting 1.5 hours. Funding will cover coaches fees, facility hire and equipment.

This project will deliver free, non-contact boxing fitness at Unity Boxing Centre for two cohorts: men 18+ and men 55+ with long-term mental health conditions. Prioritising men on low incomes and from culturally diverse communities, across 48 weeks, the charity will run four 12-week courses per cohort (eight in total). Each course provides twice weekly 60-minute sessions (maximum six men). Funding will pay for facility hire, coaching fees and promotion.

This project will run two weekly boxing and fitness sessions for inactive young people in Rotherham, aged 12 to 18. One two-hour session will be for 12 to 14-year-olds, and the other for 15 to 18-year-olds. Each session will include structured exercise, social time, and short talks to build confidence and wellbeing. Funding will contribute to coaching fees, equipment, staff training and promotion.

This project will purchase boats and blades for use by beginners when they have completed their 'learn to row' courses. the boats will be used during the club's regular training sessions, which take place three times a week.

Investment into the Place Universal Offer (PUO) will support more places in England to develop proportionate place-based whole-system approaches to tackling physical activity inequalities. It will cascade the learning from all Place partnerships and offer proportionate support in the form of tools, resources and funding required to improve the connectivity of local systems and implement systemic change.

column2: Beginner Golf Courses for wounded veterans
column3: This project will see a programme of three residential beginner golf skills courses for wounded veterans, who are at the start of their recovery, through golf pathway. Up to 16 attendees per course will receive in-depth tuition from our experienced Professional Golf Association (PGA) coaches, also including extensive time on the golf course to develop skills alongside like-minded veterans. Funding will support travel, facility hire, accommodation, coach fees and equipment.
This project will see the renovation of the current toilets. The club will convert the male toilets into a shared facility to accommodate the growing ladies and disabled participation.

This project will provide yoga for adults with learning disabilities. Weekly sessions will each last 45 minutes. There will be an initial 6-week programme followed by continuing weekly sessions. Funding will be for equipment and travel costs.

column2: Bradford Refugee and Asylum Voice Equality (BRAVE)
column3: This project will be delivered by people with lived experience of the asylum system in Bradford. Sessions will include 4 blocks of 6 weekly sessions (2 blocks for men, 2 for women). 12 people will attend each block. Weekly dance classes for 20 women, and weekly sports for 30/40 children throughout the year at the already established 'welcome group'. The project will also see a Family Sports Day for 50-60 people. Funding will support facility hire, travel and coach fees.

This project will deliver sessions of adapted sports, for people with mobility issues. Two 1 hour sessions will be delivered weekly for 6 months. A community engagement event will also be delivered and a coach will gain a coaching qualification. Funds will cover training, equipment, promotion, coaches, project management.
This project will improve pitch safety and accessibility. This will be achieved by purchasing maintenance equipment, creating a standing area for parents/spectators and clearing the grounds.
This project will rebuild the skatepark. Funding will support the contractor to install the material to build the skatepark.

column2: Active Women, Connecting Communities:Multi-Sport at Horsfall
column3: This project will run weekly women-only multi-sport sessions at the Horsfall Community Stadium. Each week there will be 1 low-impact fitness or dance session and 1 multi-sport or walking football/cricket taster lasting 60-75 minutes. 120 participants will benefit. Funding is required for coaches fees, equipment and promotion.

This project will include basketball, circuit classes, multi-skill coaching sessions, boxercise and football sessions for both girls and boys aged 11-16 living in Tonbridge and Malling. Qualified coaches will deliver the sessions and this project will be accessible to all. The project will be delivered in 1 hour sessions, 6 times per week, over a 50 week period. Funding will support coaching costs.

This project will refurbish the boathouse at the Waterloo Lake site, enabling an increase in provision to a number of priority audiences. New initiatives to be delivered include a mixed ability session, family rowing in partnership with a local housing association and after school sessions for young people from low income families. Funding is required for works including plastering, wiring, and repainting the building and coaching costs of the new sessions.

This project will deliver free yoga sessions for women in Bradford, especially those from underrepresented communities and low-income households. One hour sessions will be delivered weekly, over 40 weeks. Funding will support training, refreshments, coach fees, equipment, promotion and facility hire.

The project will replace three-lane practice nets to increase and retain participation in cricket. The net facility will be available seven days a week, used by adult and junior players during evening and weekend training. In addition, the nets will be used during weekend disability coaching sessions and by local schools. Funding will contribute to the total cost of the works.

This project will expand sessions for 2 existing projects. Golden Raiders will expand to offer additional sessions in Barrow, Dalton-in-Furness and Walney Island. Rambling Raiders will expand to deliver in Barrow. Funding will support coaches fees, equipment and facility hire.

This project will construct new improved changing facilities and provide a safe place for females to change. The project will also include toilet facilities for people living with disabilities. The funding will go towards the facility alteration.

This project will purchase American Football equipment to create an equipment store and reduce the financial barrier to those wishing to play American Football. Funding will support the purchase of kits including helmets, shoulder pads, pants, leg pads and a practise jersey for each of the 10 players. Additionally, funding will support the purchase of 30 flag belts.

This project will fund a dedicated Sports Lead, 16 hours per week, to deliver six, two-hour weekly sports sessions for vulnerable people across Leeds, Pontefract and Wakefield. Many have experienced trauma, abuse, recent homelessness or are in addiction recovery. These sessions will include a variety of activities designed to improve physical health, build confidence, and encourage teamwork. Sessions will run over 52 weeks with funding covering staff costs.

This project will continue to deliver free, inclusive sporting activities for children aged 5-16 from low-income backgrounds in Rotherham, with a focus on supporting more girls and children with additional needs to be regularly active. Activities will include weekly community football and two multi-sports sessions, which will be tailored to different age groups (5-9 and 10-16). Sessions will run midweek after-school and during weekends for 39 weeks. Funding will cover coaching fees.

This project will offer inclusive racketball coaching for young adults with disabilities or long-term health conditions. This will be achieved by run 6 x 6-week blocks, including 12 coached sessions for groups of 12 participants. Sessions will take place twice per week lasting 80 minutes each. Funding will support coaching fees, facility hire, equipment, project management and promotion.

This project will provide 8 lead coaches with refresher training including CIMPSA qualifications, 2 volunteers will become assistant coach qualified, and 9 student mentors will be trained to volunteer for the organisation. Courses will also include refereeing, first aid, and DBS. Funding will cover the qualifications, facility hire, coaches fees and practical and theory exams.

The project will expand provision to reduce inactivity and engage a wider audience. Eight additional weekly sessions will take place at the club for 48 weeks, including two classes for pregnant and postnatal women, three adult box-fit sessions, separate low impact fitness and Pilates classes for people aged 50+, and children's box-fit for 5-10 year olds. In addition, the project will deliver two weekly after-school sessions for children, and two movement sessions in care homes for older people. In total, around 400 people are expected to take part. Funding will pay for project management, coaching fees, promotion, and equipment, including mats, gloves, boxing bags, pads and storage boxes.

This project will deliver weekly walking football sessions for individuals with Parkinson's. This will be achieved through an hour session. Funding will support facility hire, coaching fees, promotion and equipment purchases.

column2: CF - BOTC Sponsored Bounce is Back!!
column3: This project will support the purchase of new push mats and fund a Level 1 Coaching qualification to grow the club's coaching base.

This project will put on 2 sessions a week for 45 weeks. This will be a weekly LBGTQ+ and then a sensory session for those with intellectual disabilities. Costs are for coaches including training, equipment, staff, promotion and facility alteration to add sensory lighting.

This project will deliver guided walks in groups of up to 20 weekly or bi weekly. 360 degree walkthroughs for over 100 UK routes will be created including miles without stiles to provide resources for more people to go outdoors or join a supported walk. Funding will cover IT, online guide, equipment, promotion, transport/travel costs and staff costs.

column2: Dinnington RUFC Girls Rugby Development Project
column3: This project will develop a full pathway from junior girls sections (U12, U14 and U16 existing) through to the creation of a first women's U18 and senior women's teams. The project will recruit two female coaches to deliver twice weekly training sessions on Wednesdays and Sundays, two hours each over 32 weeks of the year. Funding will contribute towards coaching and some equipment and essential training costs.

This project will replace and purchase new gymnastics equipment including a recreational mini high bar with a safety mat, two coaching blocks, a foam floor beam, a floor beam and a full size competition beam, to be used by the 170 gymnasts on register, as well as local children at holiday camps.

column2: Train while they train – Free HIIT sessions for parents
column3: This project will deliver free weekly HIIT fitness sessions for parents while their children take part in sports training. Sessions will run twice per week (Wednesday evenings and Sunday mornings) at Sheffield sports ground, led by qualified instructors and designed for all abilities. Costs for facility hire, volunteers, staff costs, equipment and coaches fees requested.

The project will install upgraded heating to support participation in boxing. This will include four infrared heaters in the gym and reception, electric towel radiator in the toilet, and two electric aluminium radiators on the mezzanine level. In addition, works will include construction of a 4m stud wall and glass door between the gym and reception, to improve heat retention and comply with safety requirements. By providing a warm, comfortable environment, the project will improve the experience for members and increase energy efficiency. Funding will contribute towards the overall cost of the works.
This project will support the club's growing junior offer by purchasing additional equipment to be used in training.

This project will create a 'wellness lounge' that will deliver exercise, promote healthy eating and be a social space to those who are less active/inactive and face social isolation. The gym section will be open to all the community, and an initial booking system will be in place. GP referrals and social prescribers will have access. Funds will cover equipment.

This project will deliver multisport and gym sessions to disabled people aged 18 to 30 years old over a 40 week period with 1 x 2-hour and 1 x 3-hour sessions being provided weekly. Funding will specifically support coaching fees.

This project will deliver three 90-minute adaptable multi-sports activity sessions per week for 45 weeks, in three 15-week phases. Classes for inactive young people will take place at a central venue with indoor and outdoor facilities and good public transport links. This project will run on Monday and Thursday evenings and on Saturday mornings, with activities including basketball, dodgeball, tag rugby, rounders and ultimate frisbee. Costs will cover coaching, facility hire and equipment costs.

column2: CF - New Roof for Squash Courts and Common Area
column3: This project will replace the flat roof, currently leaking onto floors of the club's three squash courts and other indoor areas. Funding will cover contractor costs for the works.
This project will fund towards a new cricket pavilion with changing facilities and social space to be used by the club and community.

This project will deliver 3 hours of multi-coaching per month to young people who live with Autism from the Telford and Wrekin area. These sessions will provide a safe and supportive space where young people can socialise and take part in activities alongside experienced staff and families, to enable connections to be made.
column14: Telford and Wrekin Council for Voluntary Service

column3: This project will provide walking football, walking netball and walking cricket to older people. Each session will be delivered for at least 32 weeks with football provided 46 weeks of the year. Funding will support facility hire, new equipment and publicity.

This project will support the delivery of the club's Try Rugby programme for participants who want to try rugby or return to the sport. The programme runs every year in January and September with 16 coached sessions over 8 weeks. 40 participants will benefit. Funding is required to support coaches fees, additional facility hire, equipment, promotion, DBS/first aid for volunteers and transport.
column14: Brighton and Hove Sea Serpents Rugby Football Club Limited

column2: Solar Powering Increased Physical Activity in Holmfirth
column3: This project will help reduce the club's carbon emissions and support financial sustainability. This will be achieved by installing a 7-kW solar PV system with a 9.5- kWh battery to power a newly repaired clubhouse.

column2: Facilities improvement for safety and accessibility
column3: This project will involve the installation of a new dance floor, 2 studio spaces and installation of new wheelchair access ramps.

Flow and Grow is a 12-month programme of weekly trauma-informed yoga sessions for women who have completed therapeutic and educational support with EVA Women's Aid, based in Redcar and Cleveland. The project will provide a safe, women-only environment where survivors of domestic and sexual abuse can continue their recovery through gentle movement, relaxation, and social connection. Funding will support instructor time and venue hire, supporting around 30 women.

This project will provide 30 weeks of weekly after school cricket sessions at 4 primary schools across the Bradford BD2 area. The project will target inactive pupils, and have at least 25% of places for girls. Funding will cover coaching costs, equipment and training.

This project will deliver 25 weeks of 2 hour sessions for a minimum of 60 young people and adults from culturally diverse communities. Sessions will include cricket, fitness and inclusive exercise, team games, creative activities and youth leadership training. Funding will cover coaches fees, facility hire, equipment, refreshments and volunteer expenses including training.

This project will employee a juniors co-ordinator to engage new and co-ordinate existing volunteers, to enable more junior sessions to be delivered, helping to grow the junior membership. Funding will contribute towards the first year salary of the juniors co-ordinator.
This project will purchase a new mower with attachments to allow proper maintenance of the green which is to be taken on by the club from the council.

column2: Growing Women & Girls Cricket at Hunslet Nelson CC
column3: This project will grow its women and girls section through engaging girls aged 11-16 by delivering 38 weeks of 2hr training sessions. Funding will cover coaching costs, facility hire, coach qualifications and equipment.

This project is a community darts session designed to boost physical activity and social cohesion in Maltby, Rotherham. Targeting the inactive, young people and adult groups. The project includes coaching, upskilling coaching staff, and leadership for young people. Funding will cover equipment, training and leadership opportunities and outreach to ensure accessibility.

This project will deliver 90-minute multisport sessions for girls aged 7-16. Sessions will be delivered four times a week over 48 weeks and will be free, fun, non-competitive and designed around the girls' own choices and interests. Funding will support coaching time, equipment purchases and marketing costs.

column2: CF - Re-imagining Haxby’s Community Sports Courts
column3: This project will see the refurbishment of the courts at Ethel Ward Playing Fields to create a safe, inclusive multi-sport hub for netball, junior football and running. The works will include the installation of solar powered floodlights. The project will enable the club to re-launch their junior sessions and Back to Netball programme.

The project will provide regular activity for around 60 less active older people living on the Fieldhead estate in Birstall. Two coaches will deliver 52, 90-minute weekly sessions on Wednesday mornings, providing low-impact activities such as boccia, walks, table tennis, yoga, badminton, exercise and chair-based fitness. Sessions will also be supported by volunteers and include social time. Funding will pay for promotion, volunteer training and expenses, coaching fees, light refreshments, and equipment.
This project will involve the replacement of the concrete surface surrounding our outdoor pool with a safe, non-slip, hygienic surface.
column14: Lazonby and District Swimming Pool Association Limited

column3: This project will deliver sessions consisting of boxing, multisports (dodgeball, circuits, exercise and fitness, dance-based activities, and skipping) and boxercise four times a week for 90 minute sessions for 48 weeks to under-represented South Asian communities in Darnall. Funding is for coach fees, equipment and promotion.

This project will provide an activity-based residential for young carers plus additional regular activity sessions. This will be achieved through a 3-day residential and fortnightly activity sessions. Funding will support the residential, care worker, additional activities, travel and facility hire.

column2: Darfield Park Bowling Club - Watering System
column3: The project will install an environmentally sustainable watering system to maintain the green and support participation in bowls. The Pro Bowl system will use rainwater harvesting and smart controls to reduce mains-water use, improve turf quality, and increase resilience to hot, dry weather. Funding will pay for the overall cost of the works, including rainwater storage tank with pump and filtration, pop-up sprinklers, weather-responsive irrigation controller, underground pipework and control cabling.

This project will create a new Padel court. The funding will go towards facilitation alteration including a double panoramic Padel court with turf and floodlights structural foundation work, a reinforced 500mm×500mm ring beam to provide the structural foundation, installation of the court, floodlights and turf and delivery of all components.

column2: CF - Girls Just Wanna Score Runs
column3: This project will enable the club to develop a new girls section, providing weekly sessions for 8-15-year-olds led by qualified coaches. Two hybrid wickets will be installed to expand playing capacity to support this new initiative. Funding will contribute to new equipment, cricket nets, coaching fees and promotion.
column14: Thorp Arch and Boston Spa Cricket Club (TABS)

column3: This project will support the purchase and installation of 28 JA Solar 460 Watt Panels and accompanying system. Panels will reduce the club's electricity costs and savings will support keeping membership costs frozen and investment into the club's work in disability cricket. Part of the club's Environmental Action Plan with costs covering contractor costs.

column2: King George V Playing Field Improvements
column3: The project will fund comprehensive improvement and modernisation works to upgrade these facilities, enhance safety, improve accessibility; maximise usage and fully realise the outdoor recreational potential of this centrally located and strategically important community asset.

This project will launch a culturally inclusive netball initiative for women and girls from culturally diverse backgrounds in Bradford. Weekly sessions will be delivered at an accessible indoor venue. Funding is for coaching fees, facility hire, coaching qualifications, equipment and volunteer costs.
This project will see the installation of solar panels and battery storage at the community centre/rugby club. By modernising the facility, the utility bills will be reduced.

This project will deliver a free 12-month inclusive physical activity programme for inactive people from African and culturally diverse communities in Redhill and Horley. Afro Beats Movement, community fitness classes for all ages and junior football sessions for children aged 5-16 will be delivered weekly, complemented by a celebration event to highlight other opportunities available locally, benefitting 160 people. Funding will support coaching, facility hire and equipment costs.
column14: Africa Community in Surrey & Sussex C.I.C.

column3: This project will install a new all-weather wicket and nursery pitch to accommodate women's and girl's cricket in Shepley, as well as supporting some of the many other junior teams. Funding will cover the facility alteration through contractors and materials costs.

This project will provide the club with a new portable net. This will enable the club to increase its offer to juniors with 2 new teams including one girls' team and increase training opportunities for all teams. Funding will support the purchase of the mobile batting net.

column2: Race for Rebound - therapeutic exercise for disabled adults
column3: This project will see the organisation construct an on site facility that will house a rebound trampoline, associated wall padding and overhead hoist. It is expected that up to 105 rebound therapy sessions will be delivered each week, benefitting people with a range of disabilities. Funding is requested for the purchase of the trampoline and wall padding.

column2: A Reliable Pitch for an Active Rastrick
column3: This project will support the continuation of cricket for existing members by improving the cricket wicket and outfield. Funds will replace the club petrol mower with an electric alternative.

This project will extend the current small members area to accommodate over 500 users and add disability access and toilets to support use by people with disabilities. A dedicated area for all members and community groups to use when the main space is hired out for large events. 550 people will benefit. Funding is for the extension works, addition of WC and access requirements.
This project will upgrade the club's all-weather practice facility. This will be achieved by re-levelling the base and installing new enclosed netting.

column2: Park Works Community Sports Hall Refurbishment Project
column3: This project will refurbish a sports hall to create an inclusive community sports and wellbeing hub. Appropriate sports flooring, energy efficient heating and lighting and safety netting will be installed. Our funds will contribute towards the installation of two indirect gas fired radiant heaters, installation and commissioning costs and towards heating controls, safety systems and access equipment.

column2: Creating Inclusive & Modern Changing Facilities for Women
column3: This project will refurbish the women's changing rooms. This will include upgrading all services, adding new toilets, showers and private changing areas and decoration. Funding will support the refurbishment costs.

This project is a 12-month community movement project across Ulverston and the South Lakes. It supports inactive adults aged 45-85 who face barriers to physical activity, including learning disabilities, neurodiversity, mental health challenges and social isolation. Through multisport, adapted movement and fitness, participants will build confidence, increase activity levels and improve wellbeing. The project will run for 12-months, with activity delivered in 6-week blocks. Each block will focus on a particular age group, sex or demographic need. Sessions will take place weekly, typically lasting 80 minutes. Funding will support coaches fees, staff costs, facility hire and equipment.

This project will be delivered in Bradford and consist of 48 x 1.5 hour sessions of yoga, targeting menopausal women. There will also be 24 nature walks for 2.5 hours led by nature walk leaders. Funding will support project co-ordination costs, instructor costs, community hall venue hire, equipment, promotion and volunteer training and expenses.

This project will deliver inclusive multisport sessions for children and young people in Girlington. Activities will include basketball, dodgeball, volleyball and cricket. Taking place over a year long period, the project aims to increase physical activity, encourage healthier habits and support positive mental wellbeing. Funding will specifically support coaching fees, facility hire, events, refreshments, equipment and promotion.

This project will allow Hinckley Water Activities Club to purchase essential kayaks and paddle boards and invest in coach training. Sport England's funding will contribute towards purchasing three 20-foot containers, increasing the size of the launch jetty, using upcycled materials where possible and new recycled plastic decking boards, with installation carried out by the club and training for 10 people in paddleboard instructor, safeguarding, first aid, paddleboard safety and rescue courses.

This project will deliver regular, low-impact physical activity sessions in trusted local venues for adults who are currently inactive, particularly people from South Asian and other minority communities, adult Muslims, women and girls, and those living with long-term health conditions. The project will deliver four sessions per week over 40 weeks, totalling 160 sessions. Sessions will be scheduled at times identified by the community as most accessible. Funding will support coaches fees, venue hire, staff costs, equipment, training and volunteer expenses.

This project will increase the number of weekly walking, dance and nutritional sessions, to meet waiting lists and demand. 90 participants will be women from culturally diverse communities in Bradford, who face barriers and health inequalities. Funding will support facility hire, instructor, nutritionist, project management, equipment and marketing costs.

This project will deliver fitness sessions to inactive women from culturally diverse backgrounds. 3 two hour sessions will be delivered weekly for 1 year. Funds will cover coaches, equipment and promotion.

This project will see the organisation rebuild an uplift road so riding can continue year-round. Funding will cover the hire of machinery, materials for road reconstruction, fuel and consumables, health and safety signage and protective equipment, promotion of the project to local communities and staff/volunteer coordination to deliver the work safely and effectively.
This project will replace external doors and create a new accessible bathroom including disabled and baby-changing facilities.

This project will deliver 46 weeks of women-only sports sessions for girls and young women in the deprived area of Manningham, Bradford. The project will offer accessible physical activities including football, rounders, netball and badminton. Weekly sessions will run for approximately 2 hours and will be delivered in a safe, supportive environment led by qualified coaches. The programme aims to engage girls who are inactive or face barriers to participation, helping them become more physically active. Funding will support transport, admin, refreshments, promotion, coaches and equipment costs.

column2: From Try-It to Team: The Griffinettes Women & Girls Cricket
column3: This project will deliver free, weekly cricket sessions for women and girls who are currently inactive or less active. Sessions focus on fun, confidence and regular moderate-to-vigorous physical activity rather than competition. Funding will support coaches fees, facility hire and equipment.

This project will deliver a 39-week, inclusive community sports programme, offering after school multisport, family boxing and fitness, community youth boxing, and girls-only football. Funding will cover professional delivery and essential equipment. Sessions will take place at Brookfield Junior Academy.

This project will deliver 2 weekly beginner rugby sessions for children aged 5-12. One session will target inactive boys and one session will target inactive girls. Each session will include 1.5 hours of structured physical activity and will consist of non-contact, low intensity physical activity, designed for children who are not currently active, or involved in any other sports clubs. Funding is for staff costs, equipment, refreshments and volunteer support.

column2: Enabling Women and Girls’ Participation at Broad Oak CC
column3: This project will convert a former kitchen into a dedicated changing space for women and girls.
This project will refurbish the existing changing rooms and convert a new space into a multi-use area for changing and community groups. Funding will support the refurbishment costs.
column14: East Ardsley United Cricket & Athletic Club

column3: This project will deliver 40 dance and movement sessions, reaching 60 adults with disabilities who attend day centres in Leeds. All participants have a learning disability, and 40% will be older people, aged 55+. Delivery will be split into; 20 weekly sessions delivered with the same group, made up of participants from different day centres and 20 sessions split into 4 lots of 5 weekly blocks, which will engage a different set group every 5 weeks. Funding will support travel, equipment, facility hire, coach fees and staff costs.

This project will enable the club to develop girls' basketball. This will be achieved through providing a weekly session, lasting one hour, for girls only. Funding will support facility hire, upskilling of coaches, equipment purchase and promotional costs.

column2: Horley Bowling Club Internal Site and Infrastructure Improve
column3: This project will deliver safety and accessibility improvements, replacing deteriorated pathways, installing equipment to help get on and off the playing green, improving wheelchair access, and creating a dedicated spectator area. The aim of this will be to enable people to keep playing bowls, but also provide a more welcoming environment for potential new members.
This project will install an irrigation system to maintain the club's green.

This project will enable the club to maintain the rugby pitches and improve the playing environment. This will be achieved through the purchase of a new mower (plus accessories), new posts, transportable lights and a line marker.

column2: York City Netball Club expansion and inclusion plan
column3: The Club is seeking financial support to facilitate increased participation within its activities. This funding will be utilised to enable the qualification of volunteers, thereby strengthening the foundation of their volunteer base. Funding will also support coaches fees and facility hire.

This project will replace 4 table tennis tables that have become unstable. This will enable the delivery of Dignity in Dementia and social table tennis sessions to continue. Funding will support the purchase of the new tables.

This project will offer seated exercise sessions twice a month to users of the community centre, particularly older adults who are less active. 30 participants will benefit. Funding is for coaches fees and additional promotion.

column2: Leeds Hyde Park FC Sports for You
column3: This project will deliver 'Sports For You', a community football project providing three coaching sessions per week for children aged 5-16. Sessions include Saturday and Sunday mixed sessions and a mid-week girls-only session. The project will target children from low income families. Funding is for coach fees, staff costs, facility hire, equipment and volunteer expenses.

column2: CF - Repair and Replace Outdoor Nets
column3: This project will see the surface of the club's outdoor net facility repaired and the nets and surrounding chain link fence replaced. This will allow training to continue from April to September and local schools to continue to use the facility.

column2: Battery Storage for Solar Panel Installation
column3: This project will install a battery storage facility to work in conjunction with existing solar panels.

This project will deliver two new open community weekly basketball sessions in Epsom and Ewell for young people aged 11-16. Each session will last for two hours and will be delivered for 47 weeks. Funding will cover volunteer costs, staff costs, promotion, equipment, qualifications, coaches fees and facility hire.

This project will build on a previous pilot programme by expanding delivery by maintaining 5 existing weekly sessions and introducing 5 new classes. The project will deliver 10 weekly classes over 36 weeks with each course running in six week blocks. In addition 18 hours of taster sessions will be delivered to engage new participants and a new cohort of up to 10 new community trainers will be trained allowing greater participation and sustainability.

This project will run after-school multisports sessions for disadvantaged girls in Stainforth. Activities include multisports, football, dodgeball, tennis, badminton and athletics. Sessions run at the sports hall at Long Toft Primary and three sessions will be delivered each week across 45 weeks. Funding is for coach fees, facility hire and equipment.

column2: ER - Cricket Net Repairs - Storm Damage
column3: This project will repair the club's storm-damaged net facility.
This project will resurface the club's 20 year old mini tennis and pickleball tarmac court surface, to allow safe use for members and new players. Funding will support contractor costs.

column2: Women’s boxing and fitness in Redhill
column3: This project will deliver a free, women-only boxing and fitness programme at Redhill Amateur Boxing Club. Delivered by qualified female coaches, the project will run two evening sessions per week (1.5 hours each) over 40 weeks. Sessions will combine introductory boxing, fitness activities, and gym-based exercise. The project aims to engage 60-80 women, improve physical and mental wellbeing, reduce isolation, and support long-term participation through training local women as future coaches. Funding will support coaches fees, training, equipment, promotion and volunteer expenses.

This project will increase physical activity among groups who face barriers to sport, including disabled adults, older people, including those with long-term neurological conditions, and women from underrepresented backgrounds. This will be achieved by running golf-related sessions, footgolf, adapted walking groups, and social wellbeing circles. Funding will support coaching fees, transport, equipment, facility improvements, training, promotion and volunteers.
An award increase to support the additional construction costs needing to be incurred to complete the clubhouse build.
column14: North Leeds Leopards Rugby League Club
