This project will engage excluded young people across Sheffield, Rotherham and North East Derbyshire through accessible gymnastics sessions. Inclusive outreach and open access sessions will take place over 23 weeks with 5 hours each week, with twelve monthly school/youth taster sessions. Funding will cover replacement or repair of equipment, coaching fees, staff costs, volunteer development and training and promotion.
column14: City of Sheffield Gymnastics Club CIC

column3: The proposal, funded by Sport England investment, will see the development of a 16 station wellbeing suite equipped with specialist fitness equipment to support a targeted offer, a new virtual studio space and consultation/treatment rooms to enable the delivery of health and wellbeing services by partners such as the Primary Care Trust, GP Surgeries and other local trusted health partners. Accessibility to the pool will also be enhanced with the addition of a pool pod. This work will be undertaken during the planned closure ensuring minimal service disruption and best use of finite resources.

To complement the refurbishment works it is proposed to redevelop an existing space in the venue to create a 16-station wellbeing suite, a new virtual studio space and consultation and treatment rooms to be used by health partners in a bid to demedicalise hospital services and deliver health interventions in the community. There will also be general improvements to accessibility and the customer experience creating a concierge pod for self-service and improved front of house services. This work will be undertaken during the planned closure ensuring minimal service disruption and best use of finite resources.
This project will remove existing and install new flooring across 2 zones of halls in the upper floor of the EIS Sheffield.

This project will provide fencing sessions to women from culturally diverse communities in Kirklees borough, Yorkshire. 30 sessions will be delivered over a year and funding will cover equipment, facility hire and coaches fees.

This project will deliver volleyball for inactive women from low income backgrounds. 2 hour sessions will be delivered once per week for 21 weeks, along with 5 monthly recreational sessions and an open day. Funds will cover equipment, facility alteration, coach qualifications and promotion.

The ETC Programme has the mission to ensure all podium and podium potential athletes and the staff that support them have access to a World Class environment in which they can work together to meet the ever- increasing demands of elite training. The funding will support greater utilisation of software and performance analysis equipment to improve performance, increasing medal chances for LA and beyond.

The project will support School Games Organisers who work across the country to support schools in their local area: to coordinate appropriate competitive opportunities for all young people from Key Stage 2-4, to recruit, train, and deploy a suitable workforce, and to support the development of club opportunities for all young people.

This project will support 120 more adults to confidently cycle. Sessions will be open to all, but particularly focused on introducing more people on low-incomes, refugees, women and other marginalised groups to cycling. Three, two-hour sessions will be delivered weekly for three weeks per month between April and October, supporting complete beginners and people who need extra support to develop their confidence. Funding will support instructor costs.

This project will deliver multi-sport sessions for children and young people aged five to eighteen with a range of disabilities, including visual impairments, autism, learning disabilities, and physical disabilities. Sessions will run four times a week, each lasting ninety minutes, scheduled during weekday evenings and weekends to suit family routines. Funding will support promotion, equipment and coach fees.

This project will support the re-opening of a community gym through the replacement and updating of equipment. Funding will cover the cost of 2 x upright bikes with LED screens and 1 x adjustable weight machine including barbell bench press.

The project will support School Games Organisers who work across the country to support schools in their local area: to coordinate appropriate competitive opportunities for all young people from Key Stage 2-4, to recruit, train, and deploy a suitable workforce, and to support the development of club opportunities for all young people.

The project is to award funding to the School Games Organiser Network - a national network of 450 School Games Organisers employed to support, among other responsibilities, the delivery of the School Games.

The request is to upgrade the one metre diving boards, assisting podium and podium potential athletes as they prepare for LA and beyond. The upgrades will also assist in the pathway development of athletes.

This project will deliver chair-based exercise, for migrant women, who have English as second language, experiencing health challenges. This will be achieved by running weekly women-only exercise classes for 90 minutes delivered by a fitness instructor. Funding will support coaching fees, facility hire, staff costs, promotion and transport.

This project will provide new activities including boxercise (no sparring), seated exercise, walking clubs, and walking rugby to adults living with long-term health conditions, poor mental health, or limited mobility. Three 90-minute sessions each week will be delivered for 45 weeks, giving participants regular opportunities to move more, build confidence, and enjoy the positive impact of staying active together. Funding will go towards coaches fees, venue hire, equipment and publicity.
This project will see the build of an extension on the Cricket Club, the extension will be accessible and will allow for improved changing facilities. Funding will support the facility alteration.
This project will involve the installation of an automatic irrigation system at the bowling green.
column14: Hallam Grange Lawn Tennis Club Limited

column3: This project will deliver Find Your Voice's, Twist and Shout programme, in care or community setting locations in Calderdale. Each location will deliver 10 weeks of activity with each weekly session being 90 minutes in duration. Sessions will target participants with disabilities and adults in later life and will involve movement/dance exercises using multi-sensory materials and music to deliver positive physical and mental wellbeing outcomes. Funding will support coaching fees, staffing costs, promotion/publicity, equipment purchases and transport/travel costs. The project is looking to run between January 2026 and August 2026 and will be seeking to attract 215 participants.

column2: Horsforth Cricket Club - women and girls initiatives
column3: This project will establish two girls' cricket teams at U11 and U13. Weekly training sessions will take place in summer, alongside matches and ten weeks of winter training. Funding will support equipment to support the new teams, facility hire for winter training and ECB level 1 coaching for up to eight people.

This project will deliver inclusive and free weekend gymnastics sessions for children aged 5-12 and their families in Kimberworth Park and the surrounding area. The project aims to reduce inactivity, improve wellbeing, and offer a fun, structured weekend activity families can enjoy together. Running for 39 weeks, it will provide two Saturday morning sessions led by qualified coaches in a safe and welcoming environment. Costs requested for coaches and equipment.

This project will run 42 weeks of activities to young people from deprived areas. Football, cricket and badminton sessions will take place weekly, fitness sessions once weekly, and walking and cycling sessions will be offered once a week after school and weekends. 300 participants will benefit. Funding is required for facility hire, equipment, promotion, coaches fees, refreshments, support staff costs and project management/coordination.

This project will deliver 2 sports/activity sessions per week for people who are homeless, living in poverty, are in addiction recovery, or facing social isolation. Funding will cover the cost of a sports leader to deliver the activities, facility hire, equipment and admin.

column2: Wheelchair Rugby League Disability Inclusion Project
column3: This project will deliver a 6 week taster programme of wheelchair rugby, at 4 different locations/community centres. Participants will then be linked and signposted to 40 weekly sessions. Funds will cover purchase of 4 additional wheelchairs in various sizes, facility hire, transport, coaching, equipment and coaching, safeguarding and first aid qualifications.
This project will deliver weekly sessions of football to young girls. 60-90 minute sessions will be delivered weekly for 1 year. Funds will cover equipment, coaches, staff costs and promotion.
This project will deliver 4 12-week blocks of rugby activity for men with a BMI of over 30. Sessions will be weekly and last 90 minutes. Funding will support coaching fees, equipment and promotion.

The project will deliver a programme of gentle, accessible physical activity for around 60 inactive adults and older people in Holmfirth. Following pre-launch taster sessions, a qualified instructor supported by trained volunteers will lead two, one-hour weekly sessions of activity such as chair-based exercise, strength and balance, dance or pilates, delivered in six-to-eight-week blocks for 48 weeks. In addition, 36 weekly sessions for smaller groups containing participants requiring more gradual progression will take place, along with eight further pop-up taster sessions at external community venues. Funding will pay for coaching fees, DBS checks, accredited training for volunteers, volunteer expenses, project management, promotion, and equipment, including weights, resistance bands, balance aids, mats and storage.

This project will deliver free weekly basketball sessions for young people aged 7-16 living in known areas of deprivation in the Seacroft and Gipton wards in Leeds. Funding is required for coaching costs, facility hire, project management, equipment and promotion.

column2: Move for Mental Wellbeing: Small-Group Yoga, Dance & Boxing
column3: This project will provide weekly movement sessions for children aged 5-16 who struggle with confidence and anxiety, or feel overwhelmed within loud settings. Activities will include yoga, dance and non-contact boxing, and will aim to help children build resilience, confidence and a positive relationship with movement. Funding is required for staffing costs, facility hire and coaches fees.

The project will support School Games Organisers who work across the country to support schools in their local area: to coordinate appropriate competitive opportunities for all young people from Key Stage 2-4, to recruit, train, and deploy a suitable workforce, and to support the development of club opportunities for all young people.
column14: Lancaster and Heysham School Sport Network (CIC)

column3: This project will deliver sessions of boxing to young girls, from low income and culturally diverse backgrounds. Two 2 hour sessions will be delivered weekly for 45 weeks. Funds will cover coaches, equipment, promotion and refreshments.

This project will run boxing and fitness sessions for women aged 18 and over, with a focus on parents and those on low incomes. Two weekly sessions will be held lasting 90 minutes. 60 participants will benefit. Funding is required for coaches fees, promotion, equipment and staff costs.

This project will deliver multi sports for girls aged 11-16 from low income and culturally diverse backgrounds. The project will deliver multi-sports, fitness, dance, netball, football and rugby. Three 90-minute sessions will be delivered per week for 45 weeks. Funds will cover coaches, facility hire, equipment and promotion costs.

The project will deliver a touch rugby programme from March to August 2026 for around 30 LGBTQ+ participants. Following a promotional open day, a total of 20 weekly sessions will take place led by an RFU-qualified coach and supported by existing players and volunteers. Each session is expected to engage up to 20 players. Opportunities will also exist to represent the club in the National Gay Rugby UK Touch Series. Funding will pay for kit, coaching fees and travel expenses, equipment, promotion and pitch hire.
column14: Brighton and Hove Sea Serpents Rugby Football Club Limited

column3: This project will provide three, hour long, movement, multisport and fundamental activities sessions per week for 50 weeks. Two sessions will be aimed at young people, and one session will be for older people all living with disability. Funding will cover coaching costs, promotion, equipment and facility hire.

This project will deliver physiotherapist-led, inclusive exercise sessions for people in Rotherham who experience barriers to being active; including those with disabilities, long-term health conditions, and low confidence in exercise and sport. The programme will offer adapted, accessible physical activities throughout the year. Sessions will take place at Rotherham Leisure Complex and outdoors at Clifton Park, led by a specialist physiotherapist. Funding will support facility hire, coaches fees, equipment, promotion, refreshments and admin.

This project will relaunch inclusive basketball session across Sussex with weekly two hour league sessions and bi monthly community tournaments for LGBTQ+ adults and inclusive allies. Funding will contribute towards staff training, insurance, equipment, officiating and facility hire costs.

This project will provide physical activity, exercise and movement rehabilitation support to young adults living with cancer, and their families and carers. The programme offers three levels of support - from accessible educational resources, to 1-2-1 yoga, to specialist cancer-exercise rehabilitation, specifically helpful for those with complex needs or treatment-related impairments. Sessions are delivered online. Funding will support coaching costs.

column2: ETC: Glass Walls for Swim Tunnel
column3: The request is to add glass walls to the Swim Tunnel transformational impact project. The project is a partnership between TotalSim, Buckinghamshire County Council, UKSI and UK Sport. The addition of glass panels will ensure coaches and practitioners can view the swimmers from the side and enable video capture for performance analysis. The addition of glass sides will have significant and immediate impact on the disciplines of Swimming, Triathlon and Modern Pentathlon.
The request is to purchase new specification balls for use in the daily training environment in Sheffield.

This project will provide physical activity opportunities for 3 cohorts of people from disadvantaged backgrounds such as ex prisoners or people serving their license in the community for one year. Each cohort will benefit from sessions as follows - 2 x walking and hiking sessions per week, 2 x gym sessions per week, personal training x 1 per week when required, bi weekly educational workshops alternating between nutrition, physical activity and mental wellbeing. Funding will cover transport/travel costs, staff costs, equipment, coaches fees and facility hire.

This project will deliver a year-long fitness and wellbeing project for African and low-income women aged 18+, including those with lived experience of premature birth. The programme provides weekly 90-minute sessions led by a qualified Level 2 fitness coach, supported by trained volunteers. Activities include Zumba, strength and mobility training, and low-impact aerobics. Funding is required for instructor costs, facility hire, equipment, co-ordination, promotion and refreshments.

column2: Development of Pickleball at Patterdale Tennis Club
column3: This project will add two new pickleball courts to the club's facilities. This will be achieved through the cleaning of one tennis court and marking this up as two pickleball courts. Funding will support the court creation and equipment purchases.

This project will expand the number of inclusive, non-competitive community boxing fitness sessions that are delivered, including structured 6-12 week beginner courses, sessions for people living with Parkinsons and extending provision into multiple community venues. Funding is requested towards coaching fees, facility hire, equipment and promotion.

This project will target young girls aged 9-14 years old from culturally diverse communities across Bradford and Keighly running fitness and sport sessions for two hours each week day for 49 weeks. Working with 125 participants each week across 5 economically deprived school hub sites. Funding will contribute towards coaching fees and promotional costs.

This project will create an accessible walking and cycling path for both service users and the wider community. The route will feature outdoor equipment, sensory areas, reflection areas and social spaces. Funding will support the path creation.

column2: All that Jazz! Seated Tap, Ballet and Everything in between
column3: This project will expand existing delivery by adding an additional weekly seated dance session, which is to be delivered during term time only. Funding will provide coaching costs.

The project is to award funding to the School Games Organiser Network - a national network of 450 School Games Organisers employed to support, among other responsibilities, the delivery of the School Games.

This project will fund improvements at the respite cottage used by families, carers and those with mental health issues, serious illness and disabilities. The garden improvement will allow use for gentle walking, informal play and light movement in a safe, accessible setting. The project will also create indoor opportunities for movement by developing the loft space to form a games room, including table tennis equipment.
This project will install an outdoor disabled toilet along with a new shelter and benches.
The project is to refurbish Carlton Pavilion and replace the existing sports hall as part of an asset transfer to GSA Community CIC from the Local Authority.

column2: Acquisition: Barbara Hepworth, Sculpture with Colour (Oval Form) Pale Blue and Red, 1943
column3: The Hepworth Wakefield has a rare, time-pressured opportunity to save a seminal sculpture by Dame Barbara Hepworth for the nation. Sculpture with Colour (Oval Form) Pale Blue and Red (1943) has been in private ownership since its creation and only publicly displayed in the UK twice in the last 40 years, despite the exceptional insights it offers into a pivotal period in Hepworth?s artistic development. THW does not own any Hepworth sculptures from the 1940s, and the acquisition would address this significant omission in our collection. Crucially, it would ensure this important work remains in the UK for public benefit, preventing it from being exported and lost overseas. We have until the end of August 2025 to raise the significant figure of £3.78m to save this key sculpture for the nation. If successful, we will ensure it is publicly displayed in the city of Hepworth?s birth, supported by our innovative learning and public programmes, enriching engagement with her art for future generations.

column3: We have a children and young people safeguarding policy in place with an appointed safeguarding lead. All staff and volunteers working with young people must be DBS checked and undertake, at a minimum, the online Leeds Children Safeguarding Partnership Training. Employed staff are expected to attend the more advanced training courses that enable them to assess risk, be aware of how to protect young people, and know their legal responsibilities. In order to enhance safeguarding for this type of work, we: • Consider the physical environment within which any delivery will take place to ensure its appropriateness and attempt to use venues deemed to be neutral; • Adhering to our safeguarding policy for recruitment of any staff and volunteers • Obtaining parent / carer consent for participation within the younger age group; • Supervision of all activities carried out with high-risk young people • Implementing online safeguarding practices for any digitally related delivery and ensuring that staff have also completed this facet of safeguarding training. • Ensuring the young people are aware of how to report any incident and also making sure the support required is in place with a referral system to the relevant agencies in place.

The Foundation has Safeguarding and Child Protection policies in place (both reviewed in 2022), and has a Primary and Deputy Designated Safeguarding Officer. It also benefits from its close association with the football club, which also has a Safeguarding Officer and FA compliant policies. Given that the programme would take place in a school setting, its Safeguarding staff are also on hand to offer advice. All Foundation staff directly involved with the activities have current and regularly updated DBS Certificates (with Barring List) and have received Safeguarding training. The Safeguarding Policy includes definitions and terminologies, types of abuse, rules, regulations, processes and procedures, training, recruitment and DBS. It is supplemented by policies relating to Child Protection, Intimate Care, and Health and Safety. External providers are also expected to provide evidence of DBS clearance and where they are unable to provide this, are supervised by Foundation staff in the setting at all times.

All HFA staff delivering the programme are Enhanced DBS checked and all have an up to date certificate in safeguarding training. In addition, all ACE staff are first aid trained as appropriate. The funding will be used to run a local youth project - providing hot meals weekly activities including sports (basketball dodgeball football) arts and crafts cooking games and trips to local attractions for young people. The project aims to reduce loneliness and to encourage new friendships.

column2: Chai and Chat Speech and Language Therapy support
column3: The funding will be used to offer specialist Speech Therapy groups to pre-school neurodivergent children and their families.  The project also aims to train families and volunteers - leading to ongoing support and better understanding of neurodivergence among local communities.
column14: Seedlings Speech and Language Therapy CIC

column3: Funding will be used to provide specialist physical activity sessions to young children. The project aims to give every child the chance to participate in the activities they wish to do. Groups include dance martial arts cricket football drama and multi-sport. Each session will involve an overriding theme which will help the participants develop strategies and methods to deal with challenges in life.

The funding will be used to continue and develop more weekly mental health focused football sessions in new areas across Doncaster over a two year period. The project aims to bring people together through the love of football improve physical health and mental health and wellbeing.
The group will use the funding to support young people who have educational needs with the aim of helping them to fulfil their potential.

The funding will be used to run activity programmes - including arts life skills and sports - for local young people to support their health and well-being while preventing them from becoming involved in crime and anti-social behaviour.

The funding will be used to continue to provide adapted yoga classes to adults with Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (ME) Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (CFS) and related conditions. The project aims to decrease participants’ social isolation increase their wellbeing and provide them with tools for better illness management.

The funding will be used to deliver workshops and events for female and non-binary young people. The project aims to improve mental health confidence and skills as participants design and deliver the project activities.

The funding will be used to offer a weekly boxing class which will provide a safe space for men to talk as well as train.  It will also offer a weekend class for young people. This aims to improve the physical and mental health of all participants.

The funding will be used to provide a parent and toddler group for children under five in the community. The project aims to improve the social and motor development of children and reduce social isolation of parents grandparents and guardians.
column14: Parochial Church Council of St Mark's Church Newby

column3: The group will use the funding to provide wheelchair basketball sessions for the local community. This aims to remove barriers to participation reduce isolation and improve  physical and mental health.

Funding will be used to offer specialist creche sessions for babies and children while their parents attend treatment plans and support groups for drug and alcohol use. This project aims to provide a safe space for vulnerable children ensuring that families impacted by substance misuse can access support in all aspects of life.

The funding will provide a warm space for older people in the community to meet on a daily basis between January and Easter 2025 with activities such as knitting dancing arts and crafts available. The project aims to reduce loneliness and social exclusion and improve mental health and wellbeing.

The funding will be used to continue to deliver services for disadvantaged young people who are at risk of exploitation county lines and crime.  This includes their ‘Point7’ programme which shows the impact of weapon-related crime a range of diversionary activities for young people and family fun days. The project aims to support young people improve confidence and self-esteem encourage positive and healthy lifestyle choices and reduce instances of knife and gang crime.

The funding will be used to support the expansion of a community pantry - as well as a signposting service for vulnerable individuals to citywide services groups and activities. The project aims to help those most in need to maximise their income and become less dependent on charitable support.

column2: Act One Community Ownership and Transformation Project: Civic Hall Community Hub
column3: The funding will be used to employ a volunteer co-ordinator to oversee the running of the community hub. The project aims to strengthen the space which is a central point for community advice support and activities.

column2: Happy Wanderer Community Mini Bus project
column3: The funding will be used to replace a minibus which is used to transport older people and adults with disabilities to a range if community and social activities. The project aims to reduce isolation and improve mental health and wellbeing.

The funding will be used to continue and develop the group's weekly support sessions for vulnerable families. It provides a warm space where carers of young children can come together engage in social activities group discussions and creative projects that encourage families and others to bond. This aims to bring people together improve mental health and wellbeing and reduce isolation.

The funding will be used to provide healthy eating sessions with physical activities improving participants' health and wellbeing. This will also create opportunities for social interaction teamwork and building connections within the community.

column2: Sheffield Stronger Together: Uniting Cultures through Sport and Community
column3: The funding will be used to engage over 1500 residents including those from minority ethnic backgrounds through a structured schedule of weekly sports sessions monthly cultural workshops and quarterly community events. This aims to provide inclusive spaces across several locations for residents to come together and connect reduce isolation and improve physical health and wellbeing.

Funding will be used to run a 12 week digital skills programme for 30 to 60 young adults aged 18 to 30 which will equip participants them with skills for employment including negotiation critical thinking and data analysis. This will improve people's future prospects and mental wellbeing.

The funding will be used to deliver weekly community cooking sessions and monthly food parcels. This will enable participants to prepare healthy affordable Indian meals. It will also provide monthly distribution events - with meals delivered to individual households or at a social events. The project aims to support people at risk of loneliness; bring people together; help to address food insecurity; and improve cultural integration and wellbeing.

column2: Increasing volunteer bereavement support capacity for East Surrey
column3: Funding will be used to continue offering free individual and group support sessions for bereaved community members. This project aims to ensure that adults and children in need of specialist grief interventions are able to access tailored support.

column2: Helping to make Ecclesfield VE celebrations inclusive for all
column3: The funding  will support the group to hold a major community event at its local park to commemorate the 80th anniversary of VE day. This  aims to bring people together of all ages reduce isolation and improve wellbeing.

The funding will be used to restore the local community's telephone box including replacement of broken glass full repainting and fixing the door to enable it to properly close. This aims to reduce isolation and bring people together.
Funding will be used to help run a support group for people living with dementia.

The funding will be used to continue the group's support and access to activities for trans and non-binary people. The project provides a range of physical recreational and social activities with the aim of reducing isolation improve wellbeing and bring people together.

The funding will be used to employ a part-time support worker who can support the running of their accommodation and activities for young to engage in.  This project aims to improve their mental health and wellbeing and reduce isolation. .

The funding will provide inclusive outdoor activities such as allotment sessions and walking trips for people with disabilities and mobility issues. This aims to improve wellbeing social connections and reduce social isolation.

The funding will be used to deliver an after school creative arts project linked to community events during school holidays for children aged 8 to 11 and their families. The project aims to bring people together from all backgrounds with the aim of reducing isolation and improving children's development mental health and wellbeing.
column14: PHASE Worldwide (Practical Help Achieving Self Empowerment)

column3: The funding will be used to deliver social activities for older people who may be experiencing socially isolation. This project aims to bring people together and create a stronger community.

The funding will be used to carry out volunteering work to improve the local community while also encouraging people to keep fit. Activities include a running and walking group to charities they can support with duties such as litter picking warehouse tidying and leaflet drops with the aim of bringing people together improve health and wellbeing and reduce isolation.
column14: Harrogate & Area Council for Voluntary Service Limited

column3: The funding will be used to run a leadership programme aimed at empowering young people from disadvantaged backgrounds in Bradford. Through workshops on leadership public speaking teamwork and personal and career development participants will gain essential skills and confidence. They will be paired with mentors to participate in social action projects that contribute to their communities.

The funding will be used to continue running a creative laundry space to help people struggling with hygiene poverty. Attendees will be able to access a free load of laundry alongside a hot drink chat and creative activity. The project aims to relieve the community from poverty and build social connections.
The funding will refurbish this community venue - making a safer nicer more accessible space for groups to gather in.

The funding will support the HOOF (Helping Out On The Farm) project for local adults with learning disabilities. The project aims to help participants who visit the farm to live healthy happy and connected lives while benefitting from and contributing to the natural environment.

The funding will be used to run wellbeing sessions for people experiencing conditions such as anxiety and mental ill health. The project aims to improve mental health through addressing challenges such as social isolation.

The funding will support the provision of frontline services to the community - via a community hub - including a foodbank emergency accommodation for nearby residents and schoolchildren and a 'warm space' during winter.

The funding will supply the foodbank with extra clothing for children and people who are a plus size. The project aims to expand and strengthen the existing highly effective service - focusing on reaching the most vulnerable and hard-to-reach individuals.

The funding will be used to continue and develop a wider range of activities for learning disabled adults living with more complex support needs. The project aims to build new life skills increase independence develop friendships and build confidence through regular social engagement.

column2: AME FOR ROMA Community Cohesion project
column3: The funding will be used to run support sessions for local members of the Gypsy Roma Traveller community. The project aims to help people feel connected and supported and to reduce feelings of exclusion from the wider community.

The funding will be used to establish a new friendship group for people over 50 who by providing them with a space to meet and take part in mental and physical activities. This aims to bring people together reduce loneliness and isolation and improve mental wellbeing.
column14: ATHERSLEY COMMUNITY ASSOCIATION AND FOOTBALL CLUB

column3: The funding is for a two-tier programme to equip children and young adults with Down syndrome with key skills to thrive in their community. The project aims to build self-confidence and provide individuals with the ability to work and participate in society.
column14: PSDS - Providing support for children with Down syndrome and their families

column3: The funding will go towards a cookery skills programme. The project aims to bring people together to build stronger relationships reduce loneliness learn new skills and make better choices around nutrition and budgeting.

column2: Connecting and Creating as We Age.  2025 - 2026
column3: The funding is for a creative programme for marginalised communities of older people based around a new Creative Ageing Festival in Brighton. The project aims to build a community of older people from diverse backgrounds from across Brighton by reducing isolation and building connections.

The funding will be used to make improvements to the community's memorial hall and purchase new tables. This project aims to improve a space that supports the local community with activities that brings people together improves health and wellbeing and reduces isolation.

The funding will be used to help the group continue delivering tailored advice and support for unemployed and vulnerable residents aged 50 and over. This project aims to bring people together improve their mental health and wellbeing and improve future life prospects.
The funding will be used to deliver group counselling sessions with activities for people of all ages to access with the aim to promote positive mental health and improve wellbeing.
The funding will be used to provide creative and film making activities for young people who have experienced bereavement. This project aims to bring people together and create a stronger community.

column2: "All Ireland Heritage Skills Programme: Consolidating Heritage Skills"
column3:
"This is the first phase of a new heritage skills programme, which will upskill 8 craftspeople. This will augment the declining supply of skills across the British Isles and will help to mitigate risk of damage or decay to heritage assets caused by inappropriate and delayed works. 
The craftspeople will benefit from  workplace placements and training across a range of heritage skills, including stonemasonry, blacksmithing, joinery and decorative finishing, achieving National Vocational Qualification (NVQ) accreditation enhancing their economic potential. 
The outcome will be an increased supply to Northern Ireland of skilled craftspeople who can appropriately maintain and restore heritage assets across the British Isles in the public and private sectors, contributing to thriving communities. 
The programme aligns with complementary initiatives aimed at obligating the use of heritage-skilled craftspeople in tenders for public assets and grants distributed to private sector asset owners; creating a virtuous circle of skills demand and supply."

column2: "Restoration and Regeneration of Ballinderry War Memorial Hall as Living Memorial and Community Hub"
column3:
"Ballinderry War Memorial Hall, constructed in 1924, serves as a living tribute to those who sacrificed their lives in The Great War. The Hall is a Grade B1 listed building, recognized for its architectural significance and historical importance. However, the December 2022 Conditions Report highlighted the Hall’s terminal decline, with one room now derelict. Without substantial repair, the building risks falling into disuse.

The vision of the Ballinderry War Memorial Hall Management Committee is to restore and regenerate this vital community asset, ensuring it remains a thriving focal point for residents. Through comprehensive consultation, we have confirmed the strong community need for such a resource. The Hall will be repurposed to accommodate a wide range of activities, from meetings and events to cultural and educational programs, serving people of all ages. Our goal is to preserve the building’s heritage while making it a vibrant hub for future generations."
column14: Ballinderry War Memorial Hall Management Committee

column2: "The Settle to Carlisle Railway Heritage Programme"
column3:
"As 2025 is Railway 200, celebrating the 200th anniversary of the birth of the modern railway in the UK, and is also the 150th anniversary of the world famous Settle to Carlisle line opening in Yorkshire and Cumbria, we wish to carry out primary research to capture the memories of residents who have lived near current and former stations on the line.

This will be through a mixture of memory banks and one-to-one interviews, carried out by volunteers trained in research methods.  It will include what impact the railway had on these communties as well as the affect of the station closures, recording people's stories to preserve for for posterity.  

The project will result in a series of 21 short videos on the history of all the current and former stations from Settle Junction to Carlisle Citadel, which will be shared for free on our YouTube channel and Facebook page."

column2: "From roots to shoots, and bricks to candlesticks - showcasing heritage learning experiences within a Victorian Walled Garden setting"
column3:
"On the hill, 1/4 mile from our main organisational site is an 1850’s Walled Kitchen Garden, formerly part of a Grade II listed estate, that has been neglected since the 1960’s. 
We want to use this unusual and unique setting to showcase heritage learning experiences and help to reconnect local people to the heritage of the Walled Garden, traditional skills/crafts, and the land.  Within this new ‘Community Garden’ space we will welcome over 200 people a year engaging in activities ranging from the practical (heritage masonry), horticultural (growing traditional food from seed, from land to plate), learning local heritage skills and crafts (candle making, willow weaving etc), and investigating/sharing the stories and history of the Walled Garden.  We will preserve the natural & built heritage of the Garden to create a place where the past meets the present, and we can help create a more heritage and environmentally conscious future."

"#LC Landscape Connections: Jewels of the Dales"
column3:
"Our project will revitalise the wildflower-rich landscapes of the Yorkshire Dales by supporting “sweet spot” farming — where profitable agriculture works with nature. Additionally, we’ll deliver targeted conservation works to restore some of the Dales’ rarest species — altogether, the ‘Jewels of the Dales’.
Development work will identify 10–15 clusters of upland farms already demonstrating good practice in nature-friendly farming. These clusters will form the foundation of our approach, complimented by the identification of niche habitat areas which require specialised conservation intervention.
We’ll map Landscape Recovery and other environmental initiatives, working with partners to align efforts — creating a more connected, resilient landscape in line with Lawton’s principles of “bigger, better, more joined-up”.
Finally, we’ll co-design trial Access and Engagement plans with farmers, developing new ways for people to experience and value this landscape. This will include outreach to schools and under-served community groups, building a long-term legacy.

"Through the project at the United Reformed Church (URC) the custodians will gain an accurate understanding of the current condition of the site and a sustainable community use will be determined. The building is Grade II* and on Historic England’s Heritage at Risk register, through updated structural and condition surveys an informed approach to future repair works, specifications, and costings for the repairs will be guaranteed. 

An options appraisal and feasibility study will look at opportunities for beneficial community uses, whilst a community audit will be used to see what engagement will benefit the community. This will allow for an informed approach to the next phase of comprehensive repair works, personalised not only by the condition but most effective usage.

This in combination with the emergency repairs will safeguard the site until the next project phase, which will be applied for at the end of the culmination of the project."

"The story of the Royal Knaresborough Forest as hunting domain for Medieval Kings is well known. Much less is known about the story of the foresters who lived under strict Forest Law and eked out a living there.  In this project, Knaresborough Museum Association (KMA) aims to tell the forgotten story of the foresters and explore what remains of the forest today in a unique and immersive exhibition, which will be held at Knaresborough Heritage Centre. 

Much of the fauna and flora within our local ancient woodland are rare or endangered, and face a  number of challenges and risks into the future.   

This project aims to engage with the local community, particularly young people, photographers and sound recordists in exploring and recreating through photography, sound, art and sculpture what is special about our local, historically significant and ecologically diverse woodland, and how we can protect it."

"This integrated nature and accessibility project will transform Plantlife's approach to inclusion. As a UK conservation charity, we recognise the urgent need to address unequal access to high quality natural heritage. Focused on our Three Hagges Woodmeadow Nature Reserve in North Yorkshire, we will improve physical accessibility to nature on the reserve for people with disabilities.  Through this project, we will also work with those with lived experience to test and refine new ways of working with volunteers, and visitors to make our reserves more welcoming and inclusive. The lessons we learn will shape how Plantlife engages people across our key nature reserves and will be shared to support wider change in the conservation sector. 

Outcomes: 

More people connect with nature through improved access, interpretation, and biodiversity at Three Hagges Woodmeadow.  
 
Plantlife builds the skills and understanding needed to better involve diverse audiences in volunteering and nature-based activities."

column3: "Hear Us Now: Voices of Mencap will capture and preserve the stories, past and present, of children with a learning disability and their families who have attended the Mencap Nursery since it first opened in 1969. As Mencap NI celebrates its 60th anniversary in 2025, our goal is to create a lasting, accessible archive of lived experiences that reflect the progress, challenges and achievements of people with a learning disability across generations. We want to ensure these important voices are heard, valued and shared before they are lost. Through this project, we aim to build understanding, promote inclusion, and strengthen cultural recognition of the learning disability community in Northern Ireland. The legacy will be an inspiring and educational resource for families, educators, researchers and the wider public, celebrating resilience and driving continued progress in equality and representation."

"We will create a lasting legacy for the Fewston Assemblage (FA) by conserving its heritage, sharing with others, engaging learners, celebrating its achievements and inspiring new work. This will also secure the original investment.

This legacy will be achieved through establishing a coherent FA collection and digitally sharing this collection of osteological and social history findings with a broader audience. Access is limited at present to those who visit the Washburn Heritage Centre (WHC) or its website.
We will complete the research and incorporate the significant research which has taken place since our last project was completed. To engage new audiences, innovative interpretation and educational resources will be developed.
Our first project  'Churchyard Secrets Revealed' has received significant global praise from academic institutions and the general public; by documenting the process and sharing it we will influence and support other projects to deliver best practice."

column2: "St Michael: The Church in the Market Place"
column3:
"Through this project, St Michael’s PCC aims to safeguard the historic fabric of the church in Malton, North Yorkshire, celebrating its religious heritage and strengthening its role within the town. The conservation works will protect the clerestory, roof, windows, and internal plasterwork, ensuring the survival of the church’s historic character and medieval craftsmanship. Alongside these repairs, the project will raise awareness of the church’s heritage, including its monuments, Victorian stained glass, and architectural features, making them accessible to a wider audience through research, interpretation, and digital resources.
This project represents a first phase in securing the long-term use of the church as a place of worship, community, and welcome to all. By fostering engagement and inclusion through multilingual welcome guides, school resources, handling materials, and opportunities to witness conservation in action, the project supports good stewardship and helps embed the church as a valued spiritual, historic, educational, and cultural asset."

column2: "Shared Heritage Futures: An All-Ireland Skills Project"
column3: "This project is a cross-border partnership between five not-for-profit organisations in GB, Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland, which aims to forward a shared approach to training in and promotion of heritage skills to benefit people and places on the island. This project builds on the All-Ireland Heritage Skills Programme (Consolidating Heritage Skills) project submitted to The Heritage Fund in January 2025, and applies learnings from this and previous interventions by project partners. The purpose of this project is to increase awareness and availability of heritage skills, to allow a more diverse range of participants, attract new entrants and provide a pipeline of candidates for future years of the training programme. This will be achieved through a four stranded approach, industry upskilling, new industry engagement, public engagement and sectoral sustainability. This will support intangible heritage and ensure that craft skills are available to care for our historic built environment."

column2: "“Sea Story”: Protecting Whitby’s Marine Heritage Through Education & Community Engagement By Capturing, Curating and Sharing Local Stories"
column3:
"Whitby is awash with seafaring history. Ships have set sail from our shores for centuries, and our striking coastline and the ocean that laps it hold an abundance of extraordinary marine biodiversity - including the majestic lobster who can live for up to 100 years.

Yet our rich maritime past and sea life, are at risk of being forgotten and diminished.  

“Sea Story” is a journey through the generations. It will explore the local heritage of our seafaring town, capturing, curating, and sharing oral histories to deepen connections to Whitby’s fascinating fishing past and inspire action to safeguard our seas.

Through intergenerational storytelling, interactive educational resources for young learners,  and inclusive, community events that spark curiosity,  “Sea Story” will capture the memories of local residents to build a living archive of knowledge and pride - a shared story ensuring Whitby’s heritage is celebrated and preserved for generations to come."

column2: "Un-Shuttered – LGBTQ+ Histories Hidden in Plain Sight"
column3:
"Through Un-Shuttered – LGBTQ+ Histories Hidden in Plain Sight, Radiate Arts aims to reveal, record and share LGBTQ+ heritage that is often overlooked within Chester’s historic landscape. The project will support LGBTQ+ people and allies to explore meaningful places through outdoor photography workshops, guided walks and a short reflective writing course, capturing personal stories, memories and lived experiences connected to Pride, belonging and community.
By combining photography with reflective writing, participants will create images and first-person narratives that uncover how LGBTQ+ histories are embedded in Chester’s streets, gardens, buildings and social spaces. These creative outputs will be shared through a public exhibition and celebration, making under-represented heritage visible, accessible and valued.
The project seeks to ensure LGBTQ+ heritage is recognised as part of Chester’s past and present, while empowering participants with creative skills, confidence and a stronger sense of connection to place."

"Wildlife in Cheshire is being squeezed into smaller and smaller corners as habitats disappear. Cheshire’s Wild Network will change that story. Cheshire Wildlife Trust aims to grow a confident, skilled and connected Wild Network of people and community groups who are actively restoring nature where they live, learn and work.
We will equip individuals, schools and communities with the practical skills, knowledge and support needed to create, manage and connect wildlife-rich spaces. By focusing on transferable skills, peer learning and long-term engagement, the project will enable people to take effective, evidence-based action for nature and sustain that action beyond the life of the project.
Each person supported through the Wild Network becomes better able to influence others, share learning and inspire further action, creating a multiplying effect across Cheshire. Together, we can turn fragmented patches into thriving, connected spaces where wildlife can recover once again."

column2: "The Old Smithy and Heritage Centre Community Project"
column3: "Through the NLHF-funded repair project at The Old Smithy and Heritage Centre in Owston Ferry we, the Trust who manage the site, will widen our engagement within our community to help make the attraction sustainable. As an active trust, we regularly undertake Open Days and events, connecting the community through our industrial heritage site. During recent events a Community Audit took place, this qualitative data has been used by us to inform and tailor future events to increase inclusion, access and participation to the needs of the community throughout the repair project and beyond. The use of the attraction is now at risk due to the poor condition of the site-particularly the roof area which requires repairs and stabilisation, as well as areas of failed pointing. By safeguarding the condition of the building and increasing engagement we will promote the site and create a lasting sustainable legacy for the project."

column2: "Saint Michael’s Lodge: A Sustainable Future for an Historic Church - Data Gathering."
column3:
"This project is required to enable the applicant, The Saint Aelred's Pilgrim Trail Society CIO [TSAPTS] to i) build the resilience, capacity and governance structures required to manage the "Saint Michael’s Lodge project" for the long term, thus ensuring that this important heritage asset has a sustainable guardian and is cared for and valued for future generations and ii) gather the professional evidence, surveys and business plans required to evaluate the potential restoration and sustainable re-use of the closed Church of Saint Michael, Cold Kirby, to ensure that the building can be maintained into the future.

Without intervention, this important historic building is at risk of long-term decline and potential loss. Located at the intersection of the Cleveland Way and the Saint Aelred’s Pilgrim Trail, [SAPT] Saint Michael's presents a significant opportunity to preserve heritage and support sustainable tourism, pilgrimage and rural wellbeing through the provision of affordable overnight accommodation."

column2: "Rewet, Rewild, Reconnect: Riparian Revival for North Lincolnshire"
column3:
"North Lincolnshire Council aims to reconnect communities with the area’s lost and degraded aquatic heritage by increasing awareness, improving inclusion and creating opportunities for people to learn about local rivers, streams, ponds and riparian landscapes.

The project will focus primarily on education, community engagement and participation through schools, guided activities, volunteering and heritage interpretation. It will help residents understand how aquatic landscapes have changed, why they matter, and how they contribute to biodiversity, flood resilience, wellbeing and local identity. Consultation results show strong support for restoration, education and community involvement.

Where sufficient community support, landowner engagement and suitable opportunities exist, the project may also enable small-scale habitat restoration or natural flood management measures. Any physical works would be developed collaboratively and would support the wider objective of rebuilding long-term relationships between people, place and North Lincolnshire’s aquatic heritage."

column2: "Celebrating and Sustaining the Heritage of St Mary's Church Kirkby Fleetham"
column3: "St Mary’s Church, is a site of exceptional historic and community value, yet its heritage is increasingly at risk of being overlooked. The church contains important architectural features dating from the 12th century, including its Norman doorway and medieval interior, but these elements are not currently interpreted in ways that engage a broad audience. Awareness of its heritage—its craftsmanship, memorials, is declining. Feedback from congregation members, and community groups indicates a clear appetite for better interpretation, school activities, events, and opportunities to learn about the church’s history. At the same time, volunteer capacity is stretched, and essential knowledge about the building’s heritage is not widely shared. Without action, the ability to care for and interpret its historical features will continue to diminish. This project is needed to celebrate the heritage of St Mary’s and strengthen its long term sustainability through careful conservation of the building, improved interpretation, and community involvement."

The project empowers girls-particularly those in foster care, adopted, young carers, or from deprived backgrounds-through structured fitness, mentoring, and positive female role models. One session will focus on boxercise and empowerment workshop on confidence, body image, and emotional wellbeing with the other session being strength and conditioning. Costs requested for coaches fees, equipment and promotion.

The project will provide free non-contact boxing for up to 60 young people. Four coaches will lead two, two-hour early evening classes each week for six months. Around 20-25 participants are expected to attend each week. Funding will pay for coaching fees and equipment, including bag gloves, skipping ropes, hand wraps and bibs.

STRONG Sisters (Scunthorpe Together Resisting Ongoing Negative Grounds) delivering weekly 45-minute female-only fitness and wellbeing sessions for 40 culturally diverse girls aged 11-17 in Frodingham and Ashby Wards, Scunthorpe, areas of high deprivation and social risk. Costs include coach fees/expenses, equipment hire/purchase, promotion/publicity with in-kind facility hire, management and volunteer expenses. The aim is to increase participation, improve wellbeing, build confidence, and create a safe, culturally sensitive environment for culturally diverse girls.

This project will carry out essential clubhouse improvements, including a new toilet block, kitchen extension, and reconfigured changing rooms to create female-only facilities. The project aims to ensure the club meets league requirements and supports participation. The upgrades will benefit around 1,500 people, including junior players, senior players, and the wider community using the facilities. Funding will be used for construction and internal alterations.

This project will increase regular sports participation among asylum-seeking boys aged 14-25 in Winsford. This will be achieved by running weekly 90 minute badminton sessions. Funding will support with coaching fees, facility hire, equipment, staff costs, promotion and refreshments.

This project will deliver a Women and Girls only Box Fit Programme. 3 sessions a week will be delivered to different cohorts on Tuesday and Thursday evenings an Saturday morning. Costs requested for equipment, coach fees and training.

column2: Clifton Alliance CC - Additional cricket ground

To complete the roll-out of eVisas, which are an electronic record of immigration status accessible via GOV.UK, for the majority of immigration products by the end of 2024. eVisas have been issued to individuals granted status under the EU Settlement Scheme since 2018 and have since been extended to other routes such as the Hong Kong (BNO) Route, the Ukraine Schemes and EEA nationals coming to work or study in the UK. As part of the rollout, extant leave holders who currently use a physical document to prove their immigration status, usually in the form of an ink stamp or vignette in their passport, a biometric residence permit (BRP) or a biometric residence card (BRC) are required to transition to the digital system before their physical documents expire, by creating an online account through which they can access their eVisa.

"We want to enhance engagement and widen access to heritage for individuals across Derry City and Strabane District Council rural area, whilst also helping to grow the capacity of small rural groups to deliver such projects.   We aim to achieve this by offering small grants to rural organisations to deliver heritage projects aimed at saving heritage while also promoting inclusion and access to local heritage and increasing participation in local community based heritage projects.  Examples of projects include publishing material highlighting historic events and the social history of rural communities, place-names, establishment of new community museums and displays, researching and publishing booklets on local history within various communities, delivering workshops and classes on traditional heritage skills and recording audio stories on local history in order to capture and record oral tradition.  Through this we will instil confidence within the community and inspire the rural community to re-engage with their heritage."

column2: "Londonderry YMCA Heritage: Preserving our Past, Inspiring our Future"
column3: "This project is dedicated to preserving and celebrating the rich history of Londonderry YMCA while inspiring future generations. We will establish a secure archive to protect over 165 years of historical artifacts, focusing initially on the 40-year history at our Drumahoe site. This archive will support the creation of engaging resources, including digitised records, interactive exhibits, and a visual timeline to showcase our heritage and stimulate community appreciation for local history. A heritage committee, comprising current and past members and youth club participants, will lead the project, receiving training to develop these resources and gain valuable skills. A reunion event will reconnect past and present members, celebrating shared memories and strengthening bonds. By promoting intergenerational collaboration and educational opportunities, this project will safeguard our past while building pride and identity, ensuring Londonderry YMCA’s legacy continues to inspire and enrich the community for generations to come."

"This project is focused on Grade 1 critical repairs to St Columb's Hall and ensuring access for all to St Columb's Hall, a Grade A listed former temperance Hall in the heart of the Walled City of Derry with a powerful connection to the local community. 

- The Hall is on the Heritage at Risk register 
- It partially re-opened to the public in 2022, but remains inaccessible to those with access and inclusion needs due to deterioration of services and key aspects of the building fabric.
- The Main auditorium has been stabilised but requires urgent intervention at northern elevation in particular to ensure stage, back stage and accessible entrances are safe to use for all. 

Key tasks for the project: 
1.Provide access to St Columb's Hall for all, with a specific focus on new communities and those with access and inclusion needs 
2. Commission special theatre consultant to develop plan for the building. The plan will inform auditorium design, theatre planning, seating system design, theatre sightlines and accessibility 
3. Complete urgent works to make the building safe and accessible for all 
4. Create a financial resilience plan for long term future of the organisation
5. Unlock additional funding to purchase St Columb's Hall providing long term stability for St Columb's Hall Trust"

column2: "#HP Sir Moses Montefiore Memorial Synagogue, Grimsby"
column3: "Through the project an accurate understanding of the current condition of the Synagogue will be gained. The updated structural and condition surveys will allow an informed approach for future works and will enable accurate specification of works and costings for funding the repairs. On completion of this project, an application for the next phase of funding can be submitted using the information. This in combination with the emergency repairs will safeguard the Synagogue until the next phase of work preventing deterioration in the interim. It is also essential that the Synagogue has an asbestos survey, something that is urgently required before use can resume. Grimsby falls within one of the highest areas of poverty within the UK; by gaining insight through trial activities, events and talks we would ascertain what services and social events are lacking in the area and promote organisational sustainability through effective use of the community space."

column2: "Remembering the WHEELIE Good Times - A BeSPOKE Heritage of GY95 BMX and Urban Sports"
column3: "GY95 CIO would like to engage at least 50 disadvantaged young people and at least 500 people from the wider community in celebrating our 30th Anniversary and exploring the cultural traditions of our members and urban sports. Young people will help us to uncover and share the rich history of urban sports culture in North East Lincolnshire in particular BMX, skateboarding and roller skating. The project aims to engage young people and the wider community in a range of heritage activities including creating a website that will become a digital archive of local urban sports heritage, collecting and recording oral history and memories from members, creating a documentary film that showcases the history and culture of the group and a 30th Anniversary book for members to collect and create materials that can be exhibited at the different sites managed by GY95 to share the cultural heritage with a wider audience."

"A new Fashion Museum, welcoming 250,000 visits annually and 400,000 online, will be established in Bath city centre, within its UNESCO World Heritage Site. Saving world-class heritage, the Museum will be a catalyst for change, revitalising its Designated Collection through new gallery and learning spaces. It will inspire and challenge through fashion, exploring it as an artform and global industry, whilst celebrating the creativity of designers, makers, and wearers, and providing learning, skills, digital and wellbeing programmes. Originally opened in 1963 in Bath’s Assembly Rooms, its forced closure in 2022, led to the acquisition of the 1927 Grade II-listed Old Post Office in Bath’s historic Milsom Quarter, presenting an opportunity to reimagine a museum on the high street regenerating through culture. This £38.4m project will be an exemplar of environmental sustainability, driving socio-economic change and placemaking, supporting disadvantaged communities across the region and providing a welcoming, accessible space for all."
